title: Use the Data Dictionary to change the structure of your data collection instruments in IU REDCap
content:
In
IU REDCap
, the Data Dictionary is a spreadsheet in CSV format representing the structure of your database. Your Data Dictionary contains the metadata used to construct your data collection instruments. It captures the same information as the Online Form Editor, but displays it in a more concise format.
Each row in a Data Dictionary spreadsheet corresponds to a field in your data entry form. The order of questions in a Data Dictionary file defines the order they appear in the database.
You can use the Data Dictionary to change the structure of your data collection instruments. If you have many variables, or are using advanced functionalities (branching logic and calculated fields), use the Data Dictionary to modify your project. Changes you make with the Data Dictionary are not propagated in real time to your project; changes are not committed until you upload the modified Data Dictionary file. Changes for development databases will take effect immediately, but changes to production databases will need to be reviewed and approved by the REDCap administrator before they take effect. The new structure will apply to both new and existing records.
After the Data Dictionary has been uploaded to REDCap, a human-readable version is accessible by clicking the appropriate link at the top of the "Quick Tasks" section on the project home page. This version is called the "Codebook", and it serves as a quick reference that lets you view the attributes of any given field in the project without having to download and interpret the Data Dictionary.
If you have questions about IU
REDCap
, or need help setting up or managing an IU
REDCap
project, email IU
REDCap
Support at
redcap@iu.edu
.

title: Longitudinal projects in IU REDCap
content:
In
IU REDCap
, longitudinal projects are similar to traditional data collection projects in that multiple data entry forms are defined. However, unlike the traditional model, forms in a longitudinal project can be completed repeatedly for a single record. The longitudinal model allows any data entry page to be repeated any number of times across predefined time-points specified by the user before data is collected.
Therefore, instead of repeating a data entry form multiple times in the Data Dictionary, you can have one longitudinal project that is repeated
N
number of times.
A longitudinal project lets you define events that allow data collection forms to be used multiple times for any given database record. An event may be a temporal event in the course of your project, such as a participant visit, or a task to be performed. After you have defined events, you must designate the data entry forms for any or all events, thereby enabling the use of one form for multiple events in the same database record.
You can group your events into arms; your project may have one or more arms. Each arm can have as many events as you wish. You can use the table provided to create new events and/or arms, or modify existing ones. (One arm and one event is the initial default for all databases).
Longitudinal projects are most commonly used for collecting clinical and research data.

REDCap
, or need help setting up or managing an IU
REDCap
project, email IU

.

In

From the Data Import tool, download your Data Import Template (click
Download your Data Import Template
) and save it to your computer as a CSV file.
Open the template and enter the data you want to import. To prevent upload errors, reduce upload time, and ensure your database is processed correctly:
Do not change the Variables/Field Names in the file.
Enter only numerical values in the "dropdown" and "radio" cells.
Delete any empty rows and columns before importing the file.
When you are finished, save the file.

Select

Note:
When the file is uploaded, its data will not be imported immediately. Data will be displayed and checked for formatting errors before they are imported into the database.
Export data
Important:
If the IU
REDCap
project data you are accessing contain protected health information (
PHI
), you must treat the data as PHI, which means files must be encrypted when they are stored (at rest) and when they are transferred from one system to another (in transit). For more, see:
Recommended tools for encrypting data containing HIPAA-regulated PHI
Your legal responsibilities for protecting data containing protected health information (PHI) when using UITS Research Technologies systems and services
If you have questions about securing HIPAA-regulated research data at IU, email
securemyresearch@iu.edu
.
SecureMyResearch
provides self-service resources and one-on-one consulting to help IU researchers, faculty, and staff meet cybersecurity and compliance requirements for processing, storing, and sharing regulated and unregulated research data; for more, see
About SecureMyResearch
. To learn more about properly ensuring the safe handling of
PHI
on UITS systems, see the UITS IT Training video
Securing HIPAA Workflows on UITS Systems
. To learn about division of responsibilities for securing PHI, see
Shared responsibility model for securing PHI on UITS systems
.
In
IU REDCap
, use the Data Export tool, accessed from your project using the link in the menu on the left, to export data. The tool provides several options for exporting data, including a simple one-click option for a quick dump of all records for your project.
For granular control over data export, choose
Advanced Export
, which lets you select individual fields or entire data collection instruments for export. If you have the necessary user privileges on your project, you can use the data de-identification options to limit the amount of sensitive information that is exported.
Once you've selected all fields and optional de-identification boxes, at the bottom of the page, select
Submit
. Subsequently, a page will appear that allows you to save the files to your computer. The files are comma-delimited and may be read into SPSS, Excel, R, SAS, and other analysis packages. Project data can also be exported in CDISC ODM format. If any fields in the database are tagged as Identifiers, those particular fields will be displayed in red.
An entire REDCap project can now be exported as a single XML file (which happens to be in CDISC ODM format). The file includes events, arms, instruments, fields, project attributes, and descriptive field attachments. If the project contains data, then users can also optionally export the project data (including uploaded files) in the same XML file. This file can serve as a snapshot or backup copy of the project.
Alternatively, you can export all project data to a single PDF file. The PDF will retain the page format from your data entry or survey page, and include all data for all records for all data collection instruments.
Another data export option allows users with data export privileges to download a ZIP file containing the uploaded files for all records in the project (files uploaded to "File Upload" fields on data entry forms and/or surveys). The ZIP file will contain a folder with all the files organized by record name and variable/field name, and it will also contain an
index.html
file that lists the following attributes for the files: record name, variable/field name, original filename, and the date/time the file was uploaded.
Note:

title: About the IU VPN
content:
Table of contents
Overview
VPN at IU
Connect to the VPN
Overview
A virtual private network (VPN) allows you to temporarily create or join a private network across an existing public network by creating an encrypted tunnel between two hosts. The encryption protects the data your computer or mobile device transmits and receives over the internet, enabling secure remote access to restricted online resources.
Many public wireless networks (such as those provided by hotels and restaurants) are not encrypted, leaving transmitted data unprotected and vulnerable to electronic surveillance. Even data originating from a secure network (for example, one provided by your employer or school) may be vulnerable if they are being transmitted to another secure network over the public internet. To prevent data from being intercepted (especially confidential financial data, or data protected by federal laws, such as
FERPA
and
HIPAA
data), businesses, government offices, universities, and other institutions use VPN systems to encrypt data transmitted between their secure networks and remote users.
VPN at IU
At Indiana University,
UITS
delivers a centrally managed, fault-tolerant SSL VPN service for use by all IU campuses.
Establishing an IU VPN connection creates a secure tunnel between your off-campus computer or mobile device and the IU network, allowing you to access online services and resources that are configured to refuse connections from outside the IU network (such as
IU Print
queues, certain library databases, and most network storage devices). Also, you can use an IU VPN connection or
IUanyWare
to make a
remote desktop connection
from off campus.
Note:
Whenever you are off campus and cannot connect to an IU service, connect to the IU VPN to check whether that fixes the problem.
For more about what traffic is encrypted with IU VPN connections, see
VPN split tunneling at IU
.
Connect to the VPN
Important:
As of February 19, 2025, the process for connecting to the IU SSL VPN has changed:
Open Ivanti Secure Access:
Windows:
From the task bar, right-click the
Ivanti Secure Access
icon, and then choose
Connect
.
macOS:
From the menu bar, select the
Ivanti Secure Access
icon, choose the SSL VPN profile you created, and then
Connect
.
When you connect, you will be presented with the IU Login prompt to enter your
IU username and passphrase
.
After successfully authenticating, you will see a prompt to authenticate via Duo and should proceed as normal.
You will then see a prompt for a secondary password.
Important:
The behavior of this field has changed. This prompt will require you to enter their IU passphrase again to finalize the authentication, rather than entering
push
or any other command or code.
For the greatest reliability across the widest range of platforms and network configurations, UITS recommends using the
Ivanti Secure Access (formerly Pulse Secure)
client, where available, to connect to IU's SSL VPN.
For instructions for connecting to IU's SSL VPN, see:
Windows or macOS:
Connect to IU's SSL VPN using Ivanti Secure Access (formerly Pulse Secure) in Windows or macOS
iOS:
Connect to IU's SSL VPN with Ivanti Secure Access (formerly Pulse Secure) on an iOS device
Android mobile:
Connect to IU's SSL VPN with Ivanti Secure Access (formerly Pulse Secure) from an Android mobile device
Chromebook:
Connect to IU's SSL VPN with Ivanti Secure Access (formerly Pulse Secure) from a Chromebook
Linux:
Connect to IU's SSL VPN using Ivanti Secure Access (formerly Pulse Secure) on a 32- or 64-bit Linux workstation
Connect to IU's SSL VPN using OpenConnect on a 64-bit Linux workstation
Important:
Use the IU VPN only under one of these conditions:
If you are trying to access a service you can't get to another way.
If your local UITS support person has told you that you need to use it.
Generally, you won't need to use the VPN if you are a student. For example, you don't need a VPN connection to:
Use learning tools, such as Canvas, Zoom, or Kaltura.
Read your IU email over the web.
Work with your files in
Microsoft OneDrive at IU
or
Google at IU
My Drive
.
If you have difficulty with the VPN:
Try using
IUanyWare
(doesn't require a VPN connection).
For example, you can use IUanyWare's Remote Desktop Connection app to remote into a device on campus. Additionally, IUanyWare's Chrome browser allows you to access sites as if you were on campus.
In IUanyWare, search the available apps to find what may be helpful.
On the IU network:
You cannot connect to the VPN, as it is for off-campus use only.
If you receive a 1329 error when attempting to connect to the VPN, try connecting using a non-eduroam or non-IU Secure connection.
Note:
To ensure accountability of network communication, the
University Information Policy Office
prohibits
group accounts
from connecting to IU's SSL VPN. To make a VPN connection, you must log in using your personal
IU username and passphrase
.
UITS staff and local UITS support people:
Although group accounts cannot access the SSL VPN by default, exceptions are allowed for areas using group accounts to fulfill separation of duty requirements in the groups or two-factor realms. For more, see
Group accounts and the SSL VPN
.
If you have questions or need help, contact your campus
Support Center

It's commonly used to store course materials such as readings, the course syllabus, images embedded in content elsewhere in Canvas (for example, Pages, Discussions, Assignments, Quizzes), and other course-related information. Upload files one at a time, or in bulk using drag-and-drop or the file picker built into your operating system. Overview
EITS uses Unified Device Management (UDM) services to deploy and manage standardized operating system and software configurations (builds) for Windows and macOS workstations. For any questions or concerns not addressed in this document,
contact EITS
.
Availability
The standard EITS workstation builds are provided as a service to full-time staff members under EITS support (for use on laptops and desktops) and to teams (for use on shared workstations). EITS builds are not available for the following use cases: servers, virtual machines, test systems, and workstations used by staff who are not supported by EITS. For more information on service availability,
contact EITS
.
Maintenance windows
EITS updates EITS-managed systems weekly. Maintenance windows ensure that devices are kept up to date. During the maintenance window, EITS requests that your device be powered on with an active network connection. Devices will only automatically install updates during the maintenance window.
Note:
Updates to address actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities may be installed without notice.
macOS
The general maintenance window for macOS devices is from 8pm Thursday to 4am Friday, and from noon to midnight Saturday and Sunday. EITS uses Jamf Pro to keep EITS installed applications up to date. Operating system updates will be served through the Software Update utility built into macOS.
Note:
While macOS updates will be pushed during the maintenance window, a manual restart may be required to complete installation. Be sure to restart your computer occasionally to ensure updates are fully applied.
Windows
The general maintenance window for Windows devices is from 8pm Thursday to 4am Friday, and from noon to midnight Saturday and Sunday. EITS uses the Global Application Update Service to provide operating system and application updates.
Note:
If prompted by the Software Center to restart or snooze, note that the snooze option will only close the window. A restart will still be required when the time expires. EITS is unable to change the default time.
Important:
If a device has not been updated within 42 days, it will be placed into an extended maintenance window, where it will attempt to install updates until it is up to date. A restart may be required.
Standard builds
The following standard EITS builds are currently available.
macOS
The standard EITS build for Mac systems is based on macOS 14 (Sonoma).  New major version updates typically are adopted within one to three months of their release.

deployment. Additionally, almost any application can be manually
installed on request or is available within the Self Service application installed on our standard build.
Note:

limits to IU's storage footprint in the Google platform

s now have a
5 GB

The default Windows build is based on

UITS staff:
Common concerns
The following information is intended to address a few common concerns potential
client
s commonly have about switching to a standard EITS workstation build:
I won't have administrative rights to my computer:
By default, as the primary user on an EITS workstation, you will not be given a local
administrator account
that allows you to install software and make other changes to your workstation. However, you can request that an administrator account be provisioned for your Windows machine by first
creating an IU group account
(if you do not currently own one), and then signing the
EITS Administrator Account Agreement
. For Mac devices, after the EITS Administrator Account Agreement is signed, a local administrator account will be provisioned on the device by EITS staff.
Important:
You are responsible for using your administrator account in a secure manner. You should not enter your administrator credentials unless you are certain you are being prompted by a trusted source. If you are unsure whether a source is trusted,
contact EITS
.
The administrator account is separate from your primary, everyday-use account, and has its own username (typically
adm
abc
,  where
abc
are your initials) and passphrase. You should practice the
principle of least privilege
and avoid logging into your workstation using your administrator account credentials. Instead, log in using your primary (non-privileged) account, and then enter your administrator credentials only when necessary (that is, to perform tasks that require administrator access).
EITS builds take a long time to deploy (and I can't afford to
lose access to my workstation):
On most modern hardware, a typical rebuild takes about one business day. Usually, loaner systems are available for use during this period. Rebuilds on older, slower hardware, and ones involving large data backups may take longer than one business day. To inquire about your system,
contact EITS
.
I'll have issues using my computer off campus:
Using an EITS-built system outside the IU network will not affect usability or security. However, some minor complications may arise in the following instances, but in each case, the issue can be resolved using existing practices:
Activating Windows or
Microsoft 365
:
Because IU uses Microsoft's Key Management System for maintaining license information, your computer may display activation errors while off campus. To resolve this issue, connect to the IU VPN. Alternatively, by request, EITS can activate your software using a different method.
Logging into domain accounts:
By default, all EITS-built
systems are joined to IU's ADS environment, and you will use your
IU username and passphrase
to log into your workstation even when you are off campus. This is possible because EITS-built systems allow you to log in indefinitely using cached credentials.
Logging in after changing your passphrase:
While your system is outside the IU network (that is, off campus), it cannot access IU's Active Directory; consequently, passphrase changes cannot automatically propagate to your system. To resolve this issue, connect to the IU VPN, and then lock and unlock your workstation. For more, see
Precautions when changing your passphrase
.
Logging in for the first time:
If you are unable
to visit an EITS office to pick up your workstation, or have arranged
with your team to have it sent to you, special accommodations will
be necessary to allow you to log in for the first time. EITS will make
these arrangements with you directly.
Group policy management:
Some settings on EITS-built systems are managed via Group Policy, and any changes to Group
Policy will not reach off-campus systems. However, policies that were
in place when the system was built will still be enforced.
Furthermore, Group Policy will be updated whenever you connect to the IU VPN.
Application updates:
When warranted by a security
vulnerability, EITS will occasionally use Unified Device Management to
deploy updates for installed applications. These updates will be
delivered to any internet-connected computer, even those outside of
the IU network.
Custom team builds
If your team consistently uses applications that are
not included in the standard EITS builds, EITS can set up
a custom team build. Doing this ensures platform consistency
across your team's systems, and reduces downtime when rebuilds are needed. To request a custom team build,
contact EITS
.

title: About the Reconciler app at IU
content:
Table of contents
Overview
Access the Reconciler app
Select a match set
Review unmatched records
Understanding matches
Understanding the Matched screen
Reconciliation periods
Perform automated matches
Perform manual matches
Overview
The Reconciler app is designed to streamline and modernize the financial reconciliation process for finance teams across Indiana University by replacing manual spreadsheet work with a streamlined, automated interface. Whether you're reconciling monthly invoices, comparing transactions between systems like KFS, MMS, or IUIE, or preparing audit-ready exports, Reconciler offers a powerful and user-friendly interface tailored to your workflow.
Finance professionals often spend hours manually comparing spreadsheets, identifying mismatches, and tracking down discrepancies. Reconciler replaces these manual processes with a centralized, automated system that:
Connects directly to your data sources (via Denodo)
, including databases, data warehouses, and spreadsheets
Automates matching logic
using configurable rules for exact and near matches
Supports manual matching
with annotation and comment features for collaboration
Provides audit-ready exports
of matched and unmatched records, including notes and error resolutions
Handles large data volumes
(from 20 to more than 700 records per reconciliation) with ease
This article outlines the initial steps to begin using the app effectively. It is intended to help finance team members who:
Perform regular reconciliations between financial systems.
Review matched and unmatched records for accuracy.
Prepare documentation for audits or internal reviews.
Collaborate with teammates to resolve discrepancies.
You do not need technical expertise to use Reconciler effectively. The app is designed to shield end users from complex setup tasks, which are handled by app administrators. Your focus will be on reviewing, matching, annotating, and exporting financial data.
Access the Reconciler app
You will receive a link to the Reconciler app from your team lead or administrator. Once you open the app:
You'll land on the "Home" screen, which shows a summary of your current reconciliation period.
You'll see tiles with information on each match set that you have access to.
If you encounter access issues, such as missing match sets or permissions issues, notify your admin contact. These issues are typically resolved quickly.
Select a match set
A match set is a pair of data sources (for example, KFS and MMS) that you'll reconcile. You'll typically work with one match set at a time:
To choose a match set, select the arrow next to its name.
Each match set is pre-configured to include fields from each data source that are relevant to your work.
Review unmatched records
Unmatched records are transactions that don't yet have a corresponding match in the other data set. To begin:
On the "Unmatched" screen, you will see a scrollable grid of unmatched records from the two different data sources.
Select a record for matching, or select again to deselect.
In the bottom left, you will see a summary of all selected records; in the bottom right, you will see options to select a match type. The available types are enabled or disabled based on the records that have been selected.
Understanding matches
A match is made up of:
Two or more selected records
A match type, which categorizes why it was matched
An optional note to provide more information about the match (in some cases, these may be required)
Match types are configurable in cooperation with your application admin. They can be set up to allow different types of matches. Some may only allow one record on the left and one on the right (one-to-one). Others may allow multiples on the left or right or both, or may be single-sided.
The match types allowed for the records you have selected will be enabled or disabled based on your selection.
If notes are required for a particular match type, the "Notes" field will be outlined in red.
Understanding the Matched screen
For each match, the "Matched" screen shows :
Matched records from the left data source
Matched records from the right data source
A button to un-match records if they were matched by mistake
Detail about the match, including match type, who did the match and when, and any notes; this may be optionally shown or hidden to save screen space using the "Show Detail" checkbox)
On this screen, you have the option to filter based on the reconciliation period for the left or right table, or to particular match types. You can also filter based on text found in the data or match detail.
You also have the option to export an Excel spreadsheet of matched data.
Reconciliation periods
Reconciliation periods may be set up for some match sets. These are configured by your application admin on the creation of the match set.
They automatically classify records into time periods based on dates found in the data. This can be by month, quarter, or other date groupings. The left and right side can be filtered independently and can have their periods defined differently.
Use the period filters on the "Unmatched" or "Matched" screen to filter.
Perform automated matches
From the "Unmatched" screen, select
Start Auto Matching
. The process will occur in the background and will let you know when it is done.
You cannot perform other matches or data refreshes while auto matching is going on. An alert bar will indicate that there is an active matching session going on and will alert you when it is finished.
If the auto match does not complete after a significant period of time, contact your application admin to check whether there is an issue and to clear the lock.
Perform manual matches
On the "Unmatched" screen:
To find records, use the search box in the left or right data grids to filter your view. This will filter based on any text or numeric field in the data.
Select the records you want to match.
To de-select matches, select the record again in the data grid, and then select
Clear
in the left or right data grid; alternatively, select the
X
next to the record in the "Selected" listing in the lower right side of your screen.
Select the match type, and then select
Mark as Matched
.
The records will be removed from your screen, and you can proceed with additional matches.

title: Why a computer may not update its DDNS records
content:
Table of contents
Overview
Correct the problem
Avoid this problem
Overview
Every computer joined to the ADS domain has a computer object/account associated with it. This account has a complex password that the computer automatically manages and changes at least every 30 days. This account is a security principal, just like a user account.
Active directory DDNS is "secure" in that once a computer registers its record, only that computer or an ADS Admin can modify it. This prevents machine identify theft via DNS. It is accomplished by restricting the Access Control List on the DNS object so that only the associated computer account can modify it. (Records in ADS DNS are actually just objects in the directory and can be restricted on a per-object basis.)
Deleting a DDNS object and recreating a new one with the same name
does not
preserve the rights of the old object. When you right-click and delete a computer object, it
does
not
delete the associated DDNS record. Therefore, if a new computer comes online with the same name as an existing machine, it will not be able to modify the existing DDNS record. This issue should eventually resolve itself when the DDNS object is considered stale and deleted by the scavenging process.
Correct the problem
If you need a DDNS record to be updated,
contact Tier 2
. Be sure to include:
A short description of the problem
The name of the machine
The old IP address
The new IP address
Local UITS support people and UITS staff:
Email
Tier 2 Support
(
sct2@iu.edu
). If you have an urgent technical issue, call
Tier 2 Support
instead.
Avoid this problem
To avoid this situation, when joining a machine to ADS with the same name as a previously existing machine:
Disconnect the machine from the ADS domain and power it off.
In Active Directory Users and Computers, select the computer account you wish to modify.
Right-click the machine account, and then select
Reset
.
Wait 10 to 15 minutes to allow your changes to replicate.
Power on the system, and then join the machine to the ADS domain.
This process also allows a person to join a different machine with the same name to the domain. Using the reset method, the machine will retain the ability to update its own DDNS record, since the SID of the account didn't change.

title: Use Schedule Builder to plan your term of enrollment
content:
Important:
IU Columbus, IU East, and IU Fort Wayne, IU Kokomo, IU Northwest, IU South Bend, and IU Southeast:
For spring and summer 2026 registration, use
Stellic
rather than the instructions here. Stellic is a new easy-to-use tool to help students plan their path, track their progress toward graduation, and register in one location. See
Stellic quick start guide for students
.
IU Bloomington and IU Indianapolis:
For spring and summer 2026 registration, continue to use the SIS Student Center to register for your classes.
Table of contents
Overview
Use Schedule Builder
Work with Schedule Builder results
Validate your classes
Set your enrollment options and save
Finish enrolling for next semester
Overview
Indiana University's Interactive Graduation Planning System (
iGPS
) Schedule Builder helps you generate a workable class schedule each semester. It scans all available sections (classes) of the courses in your plan for the upcoming term, and provides you with options based on class offerings and your availability.
You can block out times when you cannot take classes, so the tool will return only classes that accommodate your schedule.
Schedule Builder does not register you for classes
. When you find a good schedule, Schedule Builder will add classes to your
Enrollment Shopping Cart
, and then route you to the
Student Center
to complete your registration for the class sections you chose.
Use Schedule Builder
Note:
Students using adaptive technologies (for example, screen readers) can navigate the iGPS Schedule Builder using the
Text Only
link in the upper-left corner of the page. For help, see
Campus accessibility resources at IU
.
Before using Schedule Builder, use the iGPS
Degree Maps tool
to create an academic plan for completing your degree. Then, when your campus's schedule of classes for the upcoming term is available, and you are term-activated (in other words, eligible to register):
Go to
iGPS Plan
. From full-plan view in iGPS, select the semester for which you want to enroll.
If you copied course placeholders into your Plan from your Degree Map, make sure to resolve the placeholders to scheduled courses. You also may have already added specific class sections for courses directly to your shopping cart. Either way, make sure you have individual courses you want to take actually selected.
You will see a
Build Schedule
button at the top of that specific term.
Note:
If you do not see
Build Schedule
:
You may not be term-activated.
Contact your campus Registrar
to confirm that you are term-activated for that semester.
You may not have any courses. Make sure you have resolved all placeholders to scheduled courses.
Your campus's schedule of classes may not be released yet.
You cannot add courses while in Schedule Builder. Before going to Schedule Builder, add any courses for which you could potentially register to your iGPS Plan. You can always deselect a course if you don't want it included before your schedules are built. You can use the back button on your browser to return to your iGPS Plan. When viewing a single upcoming term, you can add additional courses that will then be reflected in Scheduler Builder once you navigate back to it.
To start building your schedule, select
Build Schedule
.
You will be taken to the Schedule Builder landing page.
Note:
You will see an interrupt page the first time you access Schedule Builder that offers to show you the features and options available to you. If you skip this tutorial, you can return to the Tips for that page by selecting
Tips
in the upper-right corner of the landing page.
On the Schedule Builder landing page:
All the class sections or courses you had in your iGPS Plan and Shopping Cart will be imported for you, along with any classes in which you are already enrolled for the upcoming term.
Under the "Status" heading, icons are used to signify:
Enrolled (
):
Classes in which you are already enrolled for the next term
Plan (
):
Classes in your iGPS Plan
Shopping Cart (
):
Classes in your iGPS Shopping Cart
In the top right, select
Expand Filters
to set filters and preferences for Scheduler Builder to use when constructing possible combinations of your courses:
The "Class Status" global filter is set to
Open
by default, but you can change the status to include currently closed and/or waitlist sections, if needed.
The "Instruction Mode" filter lets you select preferred modes of instruction:
100% Online All
76-99% Online Interactive
Distance Synchronous Video
Hybrid-Distance Video & Online
Hybrid-On Campus & Online
In Person
Independent/Directed Study
Internship/Practica
The "Session" filter lets you select preferred sessions (for example, first or second eight-week session).
The "Unavailable Time" filter lets you specify days and times when you know you are unavailable to take classes due to other obligations, such as your work schedule, family responsibilities, and other commitments.
Note:
Adding unavailable time slots may cause some of your courses to become unavailable. When this happens, the system will warn you and identify any issues. If an unavailable time slot is optional, consider removing it. If you cannot find an available time for a class, you'll need to return to your iGPS Plan to choose a different course.
After entering unavailable time slots, check to make sure that you've selected the set of courses that most interest you. Because Schedule Builder has pulled in your Plan, Shopping Cart, and enrolled courses, you may see courses that are back-up options for your first choice. Deselect any courses you do not want Schedule Builder to include.
To select a specific class section that you want or need for a particular course, select
Select Sections
for that course to see all sections offered for the upcoming term. Select only those sections that you want to see in your Schedule Builder results.
Optionally, when viewing sections available for a course, use the class-level filters at the top of the list (just below the course number and title) to select a specific instructor or topic (if offered).
When you are finished setting filters and preferences, select
Build Schedule
.
If there are conflicts between course offerings and your unavailable time slots, you'll see pop-up notification explaining the conflict(s). If you have conflicts, resolve them by removing filters, or return to iGPS to adjust your Plan.
If you don't encounter any conflicts, you can proceed to the
Work with your Schedule Builder results
section of this document (below).
Work with your Schedule Builder results
Your Schedule Builder results will include all schedules possible for you:
To sort through the results and find the schedule that's best for you:
Use the
Sort Type
drop-down (in the top right) to choose sort options:
None
Earliest Average Start Time
Latest Average Start Time
Most Days Scheduled
(fits in four or five days)
Least Days Scheduled
(fits in two days)
Your Schedule Builder results will be re-sorted based on your selection, but the results will still contain the same number of schedules. You can see how many schedule options you have at the top of the calendar, between
<PREV
and
NEXT>
.
Toggle
Show Unavailable
off if you don't want to see unavailable time blocks on your calendar. To remove them so that they no longer impact what schedules can be built, select
Schedule
at the top of the page.
Select
(
Favorite
) to mark a schedule as a favorite so that it will be available to you if you need to log out of Schedule Builder and sign in again later.
Your academic advisor also can mark schedules as favorites for you to consider. Select
(
Favorites
) before or after building schedules, and then look for your advisor's name along with the title(s) your advisor created:
To help narrow down your top schedule choices, activate the "Compare" feature for two or more schedules, and then select
(
Compare
) to see the compared schedules. Colors are used to represent each schedule; refer to the color key at the top of the calendar. Classes shared between schedules will display in gray and indicate the schedules that share them:
Remember to mark schedules you like best as "Favorites" so you can return to them at a later time, if needed.
To see courses listed by day of the week, select
(
Calendar view
). In Calendar view, three fields will display for each class:
Class meetings times
Session date range (which is useful when you're trying to distinguish different sections or determine how your schedule may change over the course of the semester)
Catalog subject, catalog number, and topic
Online classes with no meeting times will be listed in the "Other" section at the top of the page.
Select a class to see more details.
Classes with one-time events (such as specific exam dates or semester meetings) are identified on the calendar by "Multiple Dates" displaying where the session date range normally appears (and by the paper stack icon):
Select the class to view the details, including specific event dates:
The weekly calendar can give you a good idea of how a typical week will look if you choose these classes. At the bottom of the calendar, each class is listed with horizontal bars representing the weeks of the semester the class meets. This duration of class display can help you understand how your class schedule might change over the course of the semester:
Select
(
List view
) to easily pin a course. If you identify a specific section as your top choice, you can pin it, and Schedule Builder will show you only the schedule options that include your pinned section.
Online classes with no meeting times will be listed in the "Other" section at the bottom of the page.
Select a class to see more details.
Validate your classes
Note:
Make sure to review and compare your schedule options in either
Calendar view
or
List view
before proceeding with the following steps.
When you narrow your options down to a single schedule, select
Add to Cart
, and the class sections for which you are not already registered will be listed for you to select for validation.
Schedule Builder will check that you are eligible to enroll in the class sections you selected, and will display an explanation of any validation issues it encounters. Although you can add classes with validation errors to your Shopping Cart, you will not be able to complete your enrollment if your schedule contains a class has that has a validation issue.
Note:
Only students who are in the live Schedule Builder tool will be able to do the remaining steps to enroll in classes for the term. The test environment for academic advisors and success coaches does not have any of the steps after class validation.
Set your enrollment options and save
From
Select Classes
, select
Add to Cart
to set options for enrollment.
From here:
If enrollment is full, you can add yourself to a waitlist.
For variable credit classes (like internship or independent project credits), select the number of hours for which you are enrolling.
When all options have been saved for all classes, you will see a green checkmark, and the
Add to Cart
button will be enabled.
You will return to the Schedule screen. You should see a "Success" message telling you that your selected classes were added to you Shopping Cart.
Finish enrolling for next semester
To finish your enrollment, in the top right, select
Shopping Cart
, which will move you to the Enrollment Shopping Cart page in the Student Center. Make sure you've selected the future term that you were adding classes to and not the current term, which will likely be empty at the time you are registering for the upcoming term. Because your classes are validated, you can mark the checkboxes in the Shopping Cart table, and then select
Enroll
.
You will see an Enrollment Results summary for all of the classes you wish to enroll in. If a class is not added to your schedule, the summary will identify it as an error and explain why it was left out. Furthermore, if you don't enroll in the class, it will remain in your Shopping Cart until you either resolve the offending issue or remove it.
To see your upcoming semester's schedule by day, week, or month, select
Schedule
near the top of your Shopping Cart. Once you see the calendar, navigate to the start of the next semester to view your future calendar schedule.

Any unauthorized attempt to attach a device or cable of any kind to the back of a workstation. On most STC workstations, front panel connections for headphones and USB-compliant devices are readily available for the convenience of students.
Anyone disturbing the academic environment of an STC may be asked to leave.

content:

Overview

Overview
In
Denodo
at Indiana University, developers can migrate their own resources from DEV to STG to PRD.
Development occurs in the IU Denodo Dev environments at the following URI:
DEV:
//ebidvt-dev.uits.iu.edu:9999/<your_VDB_name>
After migration, you can access Denodo views in Stage and Production at the following URIs:
STG:
//ebidvt-stg.uits.iu.edu:9999/<your_VDB_name>
PRD:
//ebidvt.uits.iu.edu:9999/<your_VDB_name>
You can read, write, and create new objects only in the DEV environment. You can view objects in STG and PRD, but you cannot alter them in those environments. The only way to get objects into STG and PRD is through the migration process.
The only way to get objects into STG and PRD is through the full VDB migration process or the selected items migration process.
This document describes full VDB process migration process. For a description of the selected items migration process, see
Migrate selected objects in Denodo at IU
.
STG access is for testers, and PRD access is for consumers. To request access for additional users or groups to STG and/or PRD, see
Use Data Delivery Apply Security to assign security to Denodo views
.
Migrate resources
Prepare to migrate:
Before migrating your resources, prepare all of your data sources and views in the virtual database (VDB) without the
_dev
suffix (this is the VDB that will migrate). All the objects in this VDB will be migrated, except the data sources. To migrate data sources, fill out the
EDSD Support Form
; under "Application", select
Denodo
, and under "Question Type", select
Request datasource migration
. Include proof of data manager approval for all data sources that contain any enterprise data; for details about data manager approval, see
Data Manager approval for Denodo and Tableau
. Migrate any new data sources before running the migration script in
step 3
below. Until the data sources are migrated, all objects that rely on those data sources will fail due to a missing dependency.
If you have a significant amount of work in progress, you should keep that in your other VDB. If you have work in progress that only you need to access, you may request a personal VDB.
Access the scheduler:
Navigate to the appropriate version of the scheduler:
Go to
https://denodo-dev.dvt.iu.edu/solution-manager-web-tool/
.
Log in with your
IU username
and
passphrase
, and then confirm your identity with
Two-Step Login (Duo)
.
Use the "Environment" drop-down to select
Stg
for the Stage scheduler.
On the
Scheduler
tile, select
Open
.
Migrate your resources to STG:
In the Stage scheduler:
Select
Jobs
in the navigation bar at the top of the display. Use the “Job” and/or “Project name” filters to find the
import <your_vdb> Dev to Stage
job. Use one of the following methods to start the job:
Select the checkbox next to the name of the job, and then select a start option from the
Start
drop-down menu in the line of icons above the results grid.
Hover at the extreme right of the row containing the name of the job (in the "Processed (Tuples/Errors)" column) until the vertical ellipses appear. Select the ellipses and choose a start option.
You should see your changes in the STG VDB within minutes.
Note:
Your job may be named
Migrate <your_vdb> Dev to Stage
, or
Migrate <your_vdb> Stage to Prod
.
Migrate to PRD:
Make sure to
test everything thoroughly on STG
before migrating your VDB to PRD. When you're ready, access the
stage scheduler
(using the instructions from
step 2
, above), and then:
Select
Job
in the navigation bar at the top of the display.
In the list of jobs, find your
import <your_vdb> Stage to Prod
job, and start it as described in
step 3
.
Important:
Consumer access privileges do not migrate between environments. If consumers need access to views in STG and/or PRD, see
Use Data Delivery Apply Security to assign security to Denodo views
.

In some cases, you may need to have different data source connections in different environments (for example, you may want the STG Denodo VDB to point to DSS1STG and PRD point to DSS1PRD).

EDSD Support Form

Note:
Currently, Excel data sources and custom data sources cannot be managed with environment-specific configurations.
Migrate web services
If you migrate web services to production or staging and the web service needs to be deployed, create a request using the
EDSD Support Form
.

EDSD Support Form
.

title: Your status with IU
content:
Your access to UITS accounts and services is dependent upon your status with Indiana University. Most services are restricted to IU students and employees (faculty and staff), while others are available to affiliates and other guests of the university. For a full list of UITS accounts and services (including IUware) and standards for eligibility, see
Computing accounts at IU
.
Student:
Once you have been admitted to IU, you are eligible to create the full suite of student computing accounts, even if you have not yet paid your enrollment fee or registered for classes. If you do not register for classes at IU, your accounts will be disabled approximately six weeks into the semester.
Student status is determined by your presence in the Student Information System (SIS), which receives its information from the registrar on each campus. If you have questions about your standing as a student, contact your
campus registrar
.
Faculty or staff:

IU Human Resources
, you will be eligible for the full suite of employee computing accounts.

Formally appointed staff members (paid or non-paid)
Appointed adjunct faculty. Instructors who teach credit or non-credit courses are considered adjunct faculty.
Instructors contracted to teach a single class. Even instructors who teach only one class for one semester, if they were hired through the official HRMS system, are eligible for full IU computing accounts and services, including downloads from IUware.
For more about accounts for official IU retirees, see
Access to IU resources for official IU retirees
.
IU affiliate:

.

account

content:
Table of contents
Overview
MTR components
Plan for deployment
Consultation/site survey

Purchase a Teams Room Pro license
Create a MTR resource account
Prepare for installation
Choose an AD security group name to manage the MTR PC

At time of installation
Manage the MTR's resource account calendar permissions
Overview
The
Microsoft Teams
Room (MTR) system is a specific hardware and software package developed by Microsoft as an AV integration solution for conference rooms. The chief benefit of the MTR is its ability to connect with a single tap to
Microsoft Teams
or Zoom meetings from its tabletop touchscreen console.  This means no more long conference numbers to remember and no complicated logins required.
MTR components
Each MTR system includes the following components:
MTR PC:
The heart of the MTR is a Windows PC running Windows 10 IoT Enterprise OS onto which is installed a purpose-built
Microsoft Teams
Room app.  The
Microsoft Teams
Room app auto-launches at startup and runs over the top of (hides) the normal Windows desktop from users.
Touchscreen console:
This small tablet sits on the tabletop and connects to the MTR PC. The touchscreen console is used to control the system: place calls, mute microphone, etc.
AV peripherals:
Front-of-room TV, USB camera, microphone(s) and loudspeaker.
MTR Resource account:
This is a dedicated and unique Active Directory account that the MTR uses to log in to the O365 cloud.  It is also the account name that users include in a Microsoft Outlook meeting request to reserve the
Microsoft Teams
Room.  When the Outlook meeting request also includes a
Microsoft Teams
or Zoom meeting URL, the MTR PC reads the meeting information from the cloud and displays it on the Touchscreen console as a tap-to-join meeting event.
Note:
In some circumstances, there may already be an existing Outlook resource calendar in place that is used to schedule the conference room.  This existing resource calendar account can be converted into a MTR resource account, so that users can continue to use the familiar calendar account name to reserve the conference room/
Microsoft Teams
Room.
Microsoft Teams
Room Pro license:
Each MTR installation requires an annual license fee (approx. $175/yr/MTR).
Optional:
At IU, UITS strongly recommends an additional AV peripheral called the Logitech Swytch, which is a device that supports Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) conferencing mode.  The Swytch features a USB cable that appears at the tabletop.  When a user plugs the Swytch USB cable into their laptop, the laptop will connect to the room TV, camera, microphones and loudspeaker, effectively allowing the user’s laptop to serve as the conferencing device while plugged in.  When the user unplugs the cable, those peripheral devices revert to the MTR PC.
Plan for deployment
Consultation/site survey
To determine the hardware that's best suited to your specific conference room, UITS recommends an onsite consultation with the UITS Learning Space Design group.
Request a consultation
.
Purchase equipment
Typical recommended hardware
Most MTR equipment packages will include the following UITS-recommended hardware. This list does not include certain AV integration items that will be specific to a particular room such as equipment rack or credenza, TV wall-mounting hardware, surface-mount cable raceway, miscellaneous cables, etc. Note too that UITS Learning Spaces may wish to place the Buy.iu order for this and other recommended hardware not listed here on the customer's behalf.
Logitech BASE
Microsoft Teams
Rooms (no AV) with Tap + Intel NUC (Mfg. part: TAPMSTBASEINT)
Heckler Stand for Logitech Tap (Mfg. part: H660-BG)
Logitech Rally Bar (for larger rooms, typically 7 or more seats)  (Mfg. part: 960-001308)
or
Rally Bar Mini (for smaller rooms, typically six or fewer seats) (Mfg. part: 960-001336)
Logitech Rally Mic Pods: Table or ceiling mount.  In general, one mic pod per two people, for example, rectangular table with four seats on a side needs two mic pods. A table with five or six seats on a side needs three mic pods. (Mfg. part: 989-000430)
Logitech Rally Mic Pod Extension Cable (Mfg. part: 952-000047) (Note that only one cable is needed per room, because the mic pods connect in daisy-chain.)
Logitech Rally Mic Pod Mount - microphone desktop mount (Mfg. part: 952-000002) (one for each mic pod)
Logitech Swytch (Mfg. part: 952-000009)
Logitech Strong - USB-C cable - USB Type A to 24 pin USB-C - 33 ft (Mfg. part: 939-001799) (one to extend the Tap Touchscreen console, and another to extend the Swytch hub)
Sony Bravia HDR Professional Display TV; specific model and size will vary depending on room, availability, and pricing.  (Typical models as of June 2023: Mfg. part: FW-85BZ40H, FW-75BZ40H, FW-65BZ40H, or FW-55BZ40H)
Purchase a
Microsoft Teams
Room Pro license
To purchase a
Microsoft Teams
Room Pro license, email Learning Spaces Support (
cthelp@iu.edu
) with subject line "Teams Room Pro License Request".  Indicate the campus-building-room number that the MTR will be installed in, and the IU account number to be used for the purchase.  Learning Spaces Support will submit a purchase requisition in Buy.iu from Dell Inc. on your behalf and will reply to indicate the Buy.iu requisition number for your records.
Note:
If the license is purchased in any month except June, the first year's license cost will be pro-rated to expire on June 30 (end of fiscal year). The IU Purchasing office uses an internal mechanism called Project Code (MTR project code:
TEAMSROOM
), which will automatically draw the annual ~$175 from that account to renew the license each July 1 so that you don't need to remember to submit a new requisition each year.
Create a MTR resource account
To create a MTR resource account, email Learning Spaces Support (
cthelp@iu.edu
) with subject line "MTR Resource Account Request".
Your email should contain the campus/building/room where the MTR will be installed.
If there is
no existing
Outlook resource calendar used to reserve your conference room
Decide what the MTR resource account name should be.  UITS recommends the name format
<Campus code>-<Building code>-<Room#>@iu.edu
(for example,
IN-IT-219@iu.edu
), but you may wish to name the system to conform to some pattern that other resource calendars in your building or department follow.
Indicate the IU username of the person that should be assigned as the owner of the MTR resource account.
Indicate the mail-enabled AD group account (also known as the FASA or Full Access Send-As permissions group account) that should be assigned as manager of the MTR resource account (for setting calendar permissions etc.)
Once you provide the above information, Learning Spaces Support will submit a request on your behalf with IU's Enterprise Microsoft Administration team (EMA) and will cc you on that request.
For more information about the FASA or Full Access Send-As permissions group account, see
Request Full Access Send-As permissions for an Exchange Online departmental/group account mailbox
.
For more information about setting calendar permissions, see
Manage Exchange resource rooms using the resource scheduling settings
.
If there is
already an existing
Outlook resource calendar used to reserve your conference room
Indicate the display name and/or alias of the existing Outlook resource calendar.
If known, indicate the IU username of the person that has been assigned as the owner of the existing resource calendar.
If known, indicate the mail-enabled AD group account (also known as the FASA or Full Access Send-As permissions group account) that is assigned as manager of that resource calendar mailbox.
Indicate a preferred date and time that you'd like the conversion of your existing resource calendar to an MTR resource calendar to occur.
Once you provide this information, Learning Spaces Support will submit a request on your behalf with IU's Enterprise Microsoft Administration team (EMA) and cc you on that request.
To prepare your local users (those who reserve the conference room using that resource calendar) for this change:
The owner or managing FASA group member should log into the existing resource calendar and export existing appointments to a backup file as described in
How to import and export calendar in resource mailbox?
After the conversion, the manager can re-import that appointments backup file.
Contact your local users and indicate that the existing resource mailbox will be converted on
XX
date to support the new
Microsoft Teams
Room system in your conference room, and that after the change is completed, they may need to:
Reschedule existing appointments with this room (in the unlikely event the FASA group manager is unable to re-import the existing appointments backup file)
Delete and re-add the resource calendar within their Outlook desktop client's
Calendar
> "Shared Calendars" list.
Notes:
The actual process that EMA employs to convert an existing resource calendar account to an MTR resource account is to delete the existing resource calendar account entirely, and then immediately re-create it as a MTR resource account using the exact same Outlook resource calendar account display name and alias.  This minimizes friction for end users who are accustomed to reserving the conference room using that familiar Outlook display name/alias.  After the conversion, when users reserve the conference room by creating a meeting request using the familiar calendar name, and their meeting request contains a
Microsoft Teams
or Zoom meeting URL, their meeting will now also display as a tap-to-join meeting event on the MTR tabletop console.
Unlike a traditional resource mailbox that has only a name, an MTR resource account has both a username and its own unique passphrase.  The EMA Team will share this username and passphrase securely with Learning Spaces Support.  When installing the MTR hardware in your room, the (Learning Spaces) technician will type the MTR resource account username and passphrase into the MTR PC's
Microsoft Teams
sign-in menu. This is a one-time operation that allows the MTR PC to sign into the Office 365 cloud. MTR resource accounts use an MS-designed method called Modern Authentication for sign-in, meaning that two-factor (Duo) authentication is not used for this account type.
Prepare for installation
Choose an AD security group name to manage the MTR PC
An individual or group must assume ongoing responsibility for managing the MTR PC itself. Ideally, an AD security group name should be designated as the administration group for the PC. You should also know this AD group name before hardware installation, so that it can be entered during the on-site MTR PC bootup and config process; see
Create, edit, or delete Access Control Management (ACM) groups
.
Prepare the MTR PC to connect to the internet
Note the MTR PC's Ethernet MAC address.
Important:
If you've purchased the Logitech BASE
Microsoft Teams
Rooms (no AV) with Tap + Intel NUC (Mfg. part:
TAPMSTBASEINT
), the MAC address of the MTR PC should be listed on a sticker on the outside of the MTR PC's cardboard shipping box. Do
not
discard the MTR PC's shipping box before noting the MAC. If you do not have the box, contact Learning Spaces Support for guidance on determining the MTR PC's MAC address.
Make note of the VLAN that the MTR will reside in if known, or: note the campus, building and data jack id that is listed on a sticker that is affixed to the data jack on the wall that the MTR PC will plug into.
Determine a machine FQDN hostname.  Typically, the hostname will closely or exactly match the MTR device account name (for example, if a device account name is
IN-IT-219@iu.edu
, the hostname can be
IN-IT-219.uits.iu.edu
.
Once you've gathered the information above, submit a DHCP Reservation request for the MTR PC; see
Request a static IP address at IU
for information and the link to the DHCP reservation request form. In the form, for "Address Type:" select
Public (not private)
.
At time of installation
If using Logitech AV peripherals (Rally Bar + SWYTCH, and Tap), connect them into the MTR PC prior to powering up the MTR PC. For illustration, see page 7 of the
Swytch Setup Guide
(PDF).
Connect the MTR PC to the network using an Ethernet cable and power on the MTR PC.
On the "Logitech Tap" screen, a "Setup" menu wizard will appear.
Accept the EULA agreement. Tap
Next
.
In the "Account" screen, enter the MTR resource account email address and passphrase.  In the "Supported meeting mode" dropdown, select
Microsoft Teams only
.  Modern Auth should be set to
enabled
.  If you do not have the MTR resource account information, just tap
Next

title: Local users and domain users in Windows
content:
Local users
In Windows, a local user is one whose username and encrypted password are stored on the computer itself. When you log in as a local user, the computer checks its own list of users and its own password file to see if you are allowed to log into the computer. The computer itself then applies all the permissions (for example, "can use the CD-ROM", "can install programs") and restrictions (for example, "cannot install programs") that are assigned to you for that computer.
Domain users
A domain user is one whose username and password are stored on a domain controller rather than the computer the user is logging into. When you log in as a domain user, the computer asks the domain controller what privileges are assigned to you. When the computer receives an appropriate response from the domain controller, it logs you in with the proper permissions and restrictions.
Domain users evolved in response to the challenges administrators face when managing large numbers of computers, peripherals (for example, printers, network storage), services, and users. When a network has a large population of users on various computers, it is difficult to maintain information for every user on each individual computer. The task of managing so many users is simplified by allowing each computer to validate access through a central source to see if each user can log in and use computing resources. With one centralized source of user info, network administrators have only a small set of computers on which to maintain user information.
Important considerations
When you log into your computer at Indiana University, if the "Log on to:" field is
ADS
, then you are logging in as a domain user. It is important to remember that if you eventually remove your computer from the domain, you will be unable to log in because the computer will not be able to access the domain controller. If you plan to remove your computer from the domain (for example, moving your computer to an off-campus location), you must create a local user. For more, see
Disable Windows ADS network settings after you leave the IU network
.

title: Why file size appears to change when you move a file from one Unix-like system to another
content:
On Unix-like (that is, Linux) systems, the
ls -s
and
du
commands both report the size of files in
blocks
. However, the length of a block can differ between
operating systems. For example, in some Unix-like operating systems,
blocks are 512
bytes
long; in others, blocks are 1 kilobyte
(KB) long.
Some Unix-like systems that restrict the amount of storage space
their users can have measure storage space in bytes rather than
blocks. If you move a file from such a system to one that measures
storage capacity in blocks, the
du
and
ls -s
commands will report a file size different
from the one reported on the previous system; however, this does not
mean the file size has actually changed.
On UITS
research supercomputers
at
Indiana University, the
du
and
ls -s
commands both report file sizes in 1-KB blocks.

Get help for Linux or Unix at IU

division of

services, including IU's
research supercomputers
and research storage systems, and the scientific,  statistical, and mathematical applications available on those systems,
contact UITS

Overview
The IU Common Build for Windows provides central management for a great number of endpoint management functions. This includes AD group policy, BitLocker, LAPS, and all SCCM settings and software. The IU Common Build adheres to a high standard of security, based on CIS Benchmarks.

Computer locations

Build process
To move workstations to the IU Common Build, local UITS support people will need to rebuild every existing workstation. The timeline for rebuilding workstations is at the discretion of the unit. For standard workstations, you can use one of two methods:
Technician instructions: IU Common Build Windows Wipe and Rebuild with Data Transfer

Standard Windows and third-party updates are deployed during the weekly maintenance window from 11pm Thursday to 5am Friday. For more, see

title: Computing accounts for IU Bloomington and IU Indianapolis student organizations
content:
Student organization accounts must be sponsored by a faculty or staff member who is ultimately responsible for the account and its use. To obtain and maintain UITS computing accounts:

Tier 2 Accounts and Student Information Systems (ASIS)
is responsible for changes of computer account ownership. To request a transfer of a group account, see

title: About computing certifications
content:
If you need help deciding which professional certification program best suits your career objectives, UITS recommends the ThoughtCo.com
Certifications
page as a resource for information about the benefits and requirements of certifications in a variety of IT fields (for example, programming, networks, cybersecurity, and system administration).
Additionally, at Indiana University, you can
explore certification and credentialing options
available through UITS IT Training and other IU educational partners.
Following are some of the most popular IT certifications, their intended audiences, and additional links to help you get started:
Microsoft software certifications:
Microsoft Certified Systems Engineer (MCSE)
: This is the most sought-after certification on the market. It tests your knowledge of the setup and maintenance of
Windows Server
networking environments. You must pass nine tests to earn this certification. Since the MCSE is so popular, a large amount of information about it is available online.
Microsoft Certified Solution Developer (MCSD)
: Often confused with the MCSE, this certification is intended primarily for experienced programmers. You must pass four tests from a multitude of options to earn this certifications. Visual Basic, C++, and FoxPro are the supported languages.
Microsoft Certified Professional (MCP)
: This certification validates your expertise on a range of Microsoft products, technologies, and solutions. You earn certification when you pass your first qualifying exam.
Microsoft Office
Specialist (MOS)
: This certification validates your proficiency with one or more
Microsoft 365
applications and is a good entry point for anyone planning to pursue higher-level certifications.
Note:
For a comprehensive overview of Microsoft certifications, see Microsoft Learning's
Online Certificate Programs
.
Hardware certifications:
CompTIAA+ certification
: This certification is a standard for entry-level service technicians. It covers the hardware and software technologies most commonly used in business and validates the skills needed for supporting complex IT infrastructures.

title: Ensure interoperability between Samba and Windows computers at IU
content:
UITS
does not support the LAN Manager (LM) and
NTLMv1
authentication
protocols on the Indiana University
Active Directory
. Nearly all Windows computers on the IU network are configured to use only NTLMv2. Windows computers on
ADS
received a policy configuring them to accept only NTLMv2; owners of Windows computers not joined to ADS can change their settings on their own, either with an executable available on
IUware
, or manually through certain console or
registry
settings.
This affects how Windows computers on the IU network access
Samba
file or printer shares on
Unix
,
Linux
, and
BSD
servers. Only recent versions of Samba can understand the NTLMv2 protocol, and by default that ability is disabled in those versions. Therefore, if you administer a server running Samba, you may see a problem with Windows clients unless you take action to avoid it.
While it's impossible to cover every configuration across every version of Unix, Linux, or BSD, the way to avoid the problem can be generalized as follows:
The server administrator must be running a version of Samba capable of handling NTLMv2 securely. UITS recommends versions
currently supported
by the Samba team.
The
smb.conf
must include a line in the Global Settings section, labeled
[global]
, that reads:
client ntlmv2 auth = yes

Get help for Linux or Unix at IU
.

title: If your computer is infected with an instant messaging (IM) Trojan
content:
Important:
To avoid viruses spread via
instant messaging
(IM), think before you click; if you receive a message out of the blue, with nothing more than a link and/or general text, do not click it. For more, see
Tips for staying safe online
.
If your computer is infected with an instant messaging (IM) Trojan, the remote attacker can, among other things, control chat sessions, send the Trojan to people on your buddy list, and perform Denial of Service (DoS) attacks using your computer.
If you're notified that your computer is sending a virus or participating in DoS attacks, immediately unplug the network cable and reformat and reinstall your operating system. Additionally, if you were running IM software while logged into your computer with
administrative rights
, any infection contracted through that software will have administrative rights also, and you will have to reformat and reinstall the operating system. It is not sufficient to simply remove the infection, because doing so will not remove any programs that may have been installed with administrative rights while the computer was compromised. For help reformatting and reinstalling your system, see:
Safely rebuild your Windows computer
Why you should reformat your hard drive and reinstall Windows after your computer is infected with a virus
It is safest to run IM software without administrative rights, as outlined in
About the principle of least privilege
. If you were following the
principle of least privilege
at the time of infection,
University Information Security Office
(UISO) at Indiana University may consider using a cleaning tool or deleting your profile instead of wiping your computer.
Note:
For recommendations about antivirus software, see
Recommended antivirus software at IU
.

sct2@iu.edu
, including:
Device manufacturer, make, and model
Service architecture (x86/x64)
Operating system (
Windows 10
)
Expected number of supported devices
Manufacturer URL for the driver pack or CAB file, if available
From PowerShell, the results of the command:
Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_ComputerSystem | Select-Object -Property Model,Manufacturer
Unusual and currently unavailable packages
The driver package is considered unusual if one or more of the following is true:
The manufacturer does not provide default support for
Windows 10
.
The driver package will be used for fewer than 10 similar devices.
The manufacturer does not supply a driver pack or CAB file.
Standard process for building devices with fewer than 10 similar devices
Build devices using a
Windows 10
image from IUware, and then either manually install the SCCM agent, or push the SCCM agent to these devices via the SCCM console.
New driver requests when the manufacturer does not supply a driver pack or CAB file
If the device cannot be built using the standard process and does not have an existing driver pack or CAB file:
Download all necessary drivers from the site.
Extract all the relevant files from the executables.
Save these files into a folder, zip the folder, and send it and a support request to
sct2@iu.edu
.

IU community:
Connect to IU's Sibelius license server
To use Sibelius at IU, you must connect to the Sibelius Network License Server. If you are located off campus, you will need to
connect to the IU VPN
.
When you launch Sibelius, choose the
Specify License Server
option, and then enter:
129.79.184.42
Only a limited number of licenses are available, so the server will assign a license to your computer each time you launch Sibelius. When you close the program, the license will return to the pool of available licenses and become available for someone else to use. When the number of concurrent users reaches the total number of available licenses, you will be unable to use Sibelius until someone else closes the program. If you leave Sibelius open and idle for more than one hour, the system may automatically disconnect you from the server.

On a client computer, open a Terminal window: From the Macintosh HD, select
Applications

Terminal

cd /Library/Application\ Support/Avid

Esc
.

.
Close the Terminal and then start Sibelius.

content:
Table of contents
Overview
Download and install MATLAB
Update your MATLAB license
Overview
Indiana University provides access to a campus-wide Total Academic Headcount (TAH) license for students, faculty, and staff. New users can download, install, and activate MATLAB from
MathWorks
.
If you have questions about using research software at Indiana University,
contact the UITS
Research Applications and Deep Learning
team
.
Download and install MATLAB
Whether you are a new or existing MATLAB user, when you are ready to download and install MATLAB, follow the steps below.
Go to
MathWorks
and create an account using your IU email address.
Go to the
MathWorks download page
.
Select
Download
for the current release; the release name typically follows the format
R<year>a
or
R<year>b
.
Choose the appropriate installer for your operating system.
Locate the downloaded installer file. It should be in the default download folder, unless you specified another location. The name of the installer file depends on your operating system:
Windows:
matlab_<release>_win64.exe
macOS:
matlab_<release>_maci64.zip
Linux:
matlab_linux_<release>.tgz
In the above examples,
<release>
represents the release number.
Start the installer:
Windows:
Double-click the installer file you downloaded to run the Windows Self-Extractor.
macOS:
Double-click the installer file you downloaded. This will extract the files and create another folder called
matlab_<release>_maci64
, where
<release>
represents the release number. Inside this folder, double-click
InstallForMacOSX
to start the installer.
Linux:
Depending on what Linux distribution you are using, move the file to either
/usr/local/src
or
/opt
(it does not matter which you choose), and then do the following steps in a terminal window to start the installation process:
cd /usr/local/src (or cd /opt)
sudo tar xf matlab_linux_<release>.tgz
cd MATHWORKS_<release>
sudo ./install
In the MathWorks installer, select
Log in with a MathWorks Account
and follow the online instructions.
When prompted, select the license you want to use.
Select the products you want to download and install.
After downloading and installing your products, keep
Activate MATLAB
selected and select
Next
.
Update your MATLAB license
The university renews the MATLAB TAH license each July; around this time your MATLAB application will begin displaying expiration warnings. To continue using MATLAB, you can either download and install the newest version (follow
steps 5-12 above
), or use the MATLAB activation client to update your license for the installed version.
To update your license:
Launch the activation client:
If MATLAB is currently activated, open the application, go to the
Home
tab, select
Help
(in the "Resources" section), mouse-over
Licensing
, and then select
Activate Software
.
If you can't open MATLAB (for example, because your license is expired or otherwise unusable), launch the activation client manually; its location varies by operating system:
Windows:
The activation client is located here:
C:\Program Files\Matlab\R20XXx\bin\winXX\activate_Matlab.exe
macOS:
In the Finder, go to
Applications
, right-click or
Cmd
-click the MATLAB icon (for example,
MATLAB_R2015b
), select
Show Package Contents
, and then open
Activate.app
.
Linux:
The activation client is located here:
/usr/local/Matlab/R20XXx/bin/activate_Matlab.sh
In the activation client, select
Activate automatically using the Internet
.
Log into your MathWorks account.
From the list of licenses, select the license you want to activate.
Confirm the activation information.
To complete the activation, select
Finish
.

content:
Table of contents
Overview
Legacy build instructions
Install RSAT features
Overview
Starting with
Windows 10
version 1809 and
Windows Server 2019
, Microsoft no longer provides Remote Server Administration Tools (RSAT) as a downloadable package; instead RSAT is available as a set of Features on Demand (FODs). For workstations running earlier versions of
Windows 10
or
Windows Server
, you can still
download the RSAT installer from the Microsoft Download Center
.
Legacy build instructions
At Indiana University, workstations built with Microsoft's System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) that are not on the
Windows Common Build
won't be able to find the RSAT features because they are not available from the IU server. To get RSAT features, you first must change your system settings to specify Microsoft Windows Update as the source for downloading features:
Press
Windows
+
r
, enter
gpedit.msc
, and then select
OK
.
Under
Computer Configuration
, expand
Administrative Templates
, and then select
System
.
In the list of
System
settings, right-click
Specify settings for optional component installation and component repair
, and then select
Edit
.
Select
Enabled
, and then, under "Options", select
Download repair content and optional features directly from Windows Update instead of Windows Server Update Services (WSUS)
.
Note:
UITS recommends having this policy enabled only while you are downloading components that are not offered by IU's SCCM service.
Select
OK
, and then close Local Group Policy Editor.
Install RSAT features
To install RSAT features, launch PowerShell as an administrator, and then use Deployment Image Servicing and Management (
DISM.exe
) with the
/add-capability
option; for example (replace
<capability_name>
with the capability name associated with the feature you want to install; to find the appropriate capability name, refer to Microsoft's
list of RSAT features
):
DISM.exe /Online /add-capability /CapabilityName:<capability_name>
Alternatively, you can add multiple features with one command; for example:
DISM.exe /Online /add-capability /CapabilityName:<capability_name1> /CapabilityName:<capability_name2>
When you install a feature that has one or more dependencies, the dependent feature(s) will be installed automatically, as well. For example, the following command installs Active Directory Domain Services and Lightweight Directory Services Tools (ADUC), Group Policy Management Tools (GPMC), and BitLocker Drive Encryption Administration Utilities (the
Bitlocker Viewer
tab in ADUC), as well as the Server Manager feature, which is a dependency for ADUC:
DISM.exe /Online /add-capability /CapabilityName:Rsat.ActiveDirectory.DS-LDS.Tools~~~~0.0.1.0 /CapabilityName:Rsat.GroupPolicy.Management.Tools~~~~0.0.1.0 /CapabilityName:Rsat.BitLocker.Recovery.Tools~~~~0.0.1.0
