title: Configure delivery pipelines
content:
Table of contents
Overview
Pull images from a private repository
Create an image pull secret
Specify an image pull secret in a manifest
Assign an image pull secret to a service account
Use a deployer service account
Spring Boot application deployments
How to use a Harbor robot account in Bamboo using a CLI
Overview
Following are instructions for automating deployments using a private registry, Kubernetes service accounts, and CD environments, such as Bamboo.
Pull images from a private repository
If you are deploying containers in Kubernetes from a private repository, you will need to configure your Kubernetes deployment with the credentials to access your private repository.
An image pull secret will allow a Kubernetes deployment to pull private images to deploy your containers. The following steps will help you configure an image pull secret for your Kubernetes deployment. You may also refer to the official
Kubernetes documentation
for further details.
Note:
This guide uses the commonly used
Deployment
manifest as an example but should apply for other manifests that support a
Pod
specification, such as
StatefulSets
and
DaemonSets
.
Create an image pull secret
To create an image pull secret in your namespace, run the following command:
kubectl create secret docker-registry
regcred
\
-
-docker-server=
your-registry-server
\
# e.g: registry.docker.iu.edu
-
-docker-username=
your-username
\
# e.g: groupacc (a group account with pull privilege only)
-
-docker-password=
your-password
\
-
-namespace=
team-namespace
# e.g: ua-vpit--enterprise-systems--mydept
The command above creates an image pull secret with the name
regcred
that you can later refer to from your
Deployment
manifest. (You may choose any easily identifiable image pull secret name to replace
regcred
in this example.)
Specify an image pull secret in a manifest
Specify the name of the image pull secret (
regcred
) that created above in the
Deployment
manifest, as shown in the following example:
apiVersion:
apps/v1
kind:
Deployment
metadata:
name:
nginx-deployment
labels:
app:
nginx
spec:
replicas:
3
selector:
matchLabels:
app:
nginx
template:
metadata:
labels:
app:
nginx
spec:
imagePullSecrets:
- name:
regcred
# Specify your Image Pull Secret name here
containers:
- name:
nginx
image:
registry.docker.iu.edu/mydept/nginx:latest
ports:
- containerPort:
80
Assign an image pull secret to a service account
Alternatively, you can assign the image pull secret you created to the service account that runs your deployment, rather than specifying it in your
Deployment
manifest. This could simplify your manifest if you have a lot of applications.
First, determine the service account that runs your deployment. By default, Kubernetes has already created a service account with the name
default
to run all your deployments in your namespace. If you configure your
Deployment
to be run by another service account, use that service account instead of
default
in the following example:
kubectl patch serviceaccount
default
\
-p '{
"imagePullSecrets"
: [{
"name"
:
"
regcred
"
}]}'
# Image Pull Secret name you create earlier
Use a deployer service account
If you requested a
deployer
service account, you should have received a Kubernetes configuration file. This file contains all of the details needed to connect to a specific cluster and perform actions as the
deployer
service account in your namespace. Generally, this file is placed in your home directory at
~/.kube/config
(for example,
bind mounted
into the container used to perform deployments in your CD environment). The following
docker run
command shows how to mount a
my.config
file on the host machine into a user's
~/.kube
directory within the container. Other CD tools, such as Bamboo, should have a volumes section to specify directories and files to mount.
docker
run
-v $(
pwd
)/my.config:/home/foobar/.kube/config
$IMAGE
$COMMAND
Once that's in place,
kubectl
will use this file to authenticate with the cluster. You may also specify a config file using the
--kubeconfig
flag on
kubectl
; for example:
kubectl --kubeconfig /path/to/my.
config
get
pods
The
deployer
account has a role binding on the
restricted-control
cluster role. See
Role-based access control (RBAC) in Kubernetes at IU
for all of the resources available. If any resources or verbs are missing that you require for your deployments, send a request to
docker@iu.edu
.
A Docker image is currently being developed to facilitate deployments. The current stable version is
registry.docker.iu.edu/library/kube-deployer:stable
and contains a supported version of
kubectl
. To use this image, mount your config file at
/root/.kube/config
. It also contains a Helm 3 binary (
helm
) if using Helm to perform deployments.
Spring Boot application deployments
For teams deploying Spring Boot applications, a
Helm chart
is available to standardize deployments.
Workflow
is an example project using this chart. Two values files are required:
helm-common.yaml
, which contains common values for all of your application environments, and an environment specific values file, for example
helm-snd.yaml
.
If using Bamboo to deploy this Spring Boot application, create a job that runs in a Docker container. Set the image to
registry.docker.iu.edu/library/helm-k8s-boot-deployer:stable
and add a couple of tasks. The first task should check out your source code. The second should be a Script task; for this task set the following:
Interpreter:
Shell
Script location:
File
Script file:
/deploy.sh
Argument:
appcode envcode namespace dockerSecret
(replace
appcode
with your application code,
envcode
with your environment code,
namespace
with your Kubernetes namespace,
dockerSecret
with registry credentials formatted as
username:password
; for example,
wrkflw snd ua-vpit--enterprise-systems--esimw foobar:mypassword
).
You will also need to ensure some volumes are present. Use the default volumes for both Host and Container directories:
${bamboo.working.directory}
and
${bamboo.tmp.directory}
. Create a third volume that mounts the
deployer
config file at
/root/.kube/config
.
The
Dockerfile
for the kube-deployer image is available in
IU GitHub
. The
deploy.sh
script baked into the image performs a
helm upgrade
on your project.
Note:
There is a known issue when running tasks in a Docker container. The image is not pulled on every run, so if the
stable
tag is updated, you may still be running on an older image. One workaround is to add a job before your deployment that pulls the docker image on a particular agent. Your deployment job should also run on the same agent.
Use a Harbor robot account in Bamboo using a CLI
This section assumes you've followed
these instructions for creating a robot account
.
Below is an example showing how to sign in, build, and push an image to Harbor using Bamboo using the Agent environment (replace
robot$foobar
with your robot account name).
Create a plan and add the repository that contains your
Dockerfile
.
Create a variable named
registryPassword
to hold the password for
robot$foobar
.
Create a stage and add a job with the following tasks:
A Source Code Checkout task for the repository containing your
Dockerfile
A Script task with the following Script body:
docker login --username=
'robot$deployer'
\
--password=
"${bamboo.registryPassword}"
registry
.docker
.iu
.edu
docker build --rm --pull \
-t registry
.docker
.iu
.edu
/your-project/your-image:some-tag .
docker push registry
.docker
.iu
.edu
/your-project/your-image:some-tag
Due to escaping issues related to the dollar sign, if you choose to use a variable for the username (for example,
registryUsername
), you will need to set it in the environment variables field like this,
REGISTRY_USERNAME
=
"${bamboo.registryUsername}"
Then, use it in the script body:
docker login --username=
"${REGISTRY_USERNAME}"
--password=
"${bamboo.registryPassword}"
registry
.docker
.iu
.edu
If you choose to build your images in a Docker container rather than the Bamboo agent environment, you will need to choose an image that has the
docker
command line tool installed (for example,
docker:19.03.8
).
You will also need to mount in the Docker socket that's available on the Bamboo agents. Under the Docker tab of a job, set the following volume where both the Host directory and the Container directory are
/var/run/docker.sock
. From that point forward, you can follow the steps above for the agent environment.

content:

If Windows is already installed on your computer
Warning:
Installing Windows via any of these methods, with the exception of refreshing, will permanently
delete all
data and desktop programs (including
Microsoft Office
and all others) from your computer. Before proceeding, back up/copy all data files (such as documents, pictures, music, and videos) to a flash drive, external hard drive, or cloud storage. Additionally, you should locate the installation media for your software and your subscription information for third-party software.
Why reinstall Windows
Important:
Microsoft
ended support for
Windows 7
on January 14, 2020. If you're using
Windows 7
, UITS strongly recommends that you upgrade to a new operating system.
Reinstall Windows if you have any of these issues:
Virus or malware infection:
If your computer has been infected with a virus, malware or other type of malicious infection, the only way to fully clean it is to back up your files and reinstall Windows. Reinstalling Windows is not the same as the Windows System Restore utility, which does not help in the case of a virus or malware infection. If your IU network access has been blocked by the
University Information Security Office
(UISO) due to a virus infection, you are required to reinstall.
Slow to the point of being unusable:
Over time (especially after a few years), any operating system can become sluggish due to changes that have occurred (such as installing/uninstalling programs). If your computer has become slow to the point of being unusable, reinstalling Windows may be the best and quickest solution. Extreme slowness may also be a symptom of infection.
General stability issues:
If you're having general stability issues such as "blue screens", unusual error messages, or other strange issues, or you've exhausted all other troubleshooting methods, it may be best to reinstall Windows.
For help, contact your campus
Support Center
.
Recycling, selling, or giving your PC away:
If your personal device will no longer be in your possession, you should reinstall Windows to remove your personal information. This does not guarantee that your personal files would not be recoverable, however. Thus, if you have sensitive data on your personal computer, UITS recommends that you
securely wipe
the disk drive. Be aware that this removes the Windows operating system and license from the device. For departmental computers, see
Departmental disposal of equipment at IU
.
Network access blocked due to rootkit:
If your network access has been blocked due to a virus infection called a rootkit, nothing mentioned here will fix the problem; UISO will email you with specific instructions for getting rid of the infection.
How to install, reinstall, or perform an in-place upgrade of Windows on a PC
Prepare for the installation process:
For security reasons, you should install Windows or rebuild your Windows computer offline (unplug your network cable), and then take certain measures to assure its security before putting it back on the network; see
Safely rebuild your Windows computer
.
Check your computer manufacturer's support site and manual (see
Additional Resources
) for the following (for the most reliable information, enter the computer's service tag or serial number where available):
Determine the optimal method(s) that your manufacturer recommends for installing Windows (since Windows is increasingly tied to the specific hardware of your computer due to security enhancements, including secure boot).
Make sure that upgrading Windows will not result in a voided warranty, loss of service and support, or lack of drivers (software that tells Windows how to manage the hardware components, such as the sound card, video card, touchpad, and others).
Make sure that your computer is compatible with the version of Windows you wish to install; see
methods below
for a guide to the various options. This is especially critical if you're doing a clean install and upgrade, such as
Windows 8
to
Windows 10
.
If you haven't already done so, back up/copy all data files (documents, pictures, music, videos) to a flash drive, external hard drive, or cloud storage.
Be aware of the settings you'll need to select during setup or immediately afterward:
Be sure of the language you wish to choose, and your time zone.
IU Northwest is on (GMT-06:00) Central Time (US & Canada). All other IU campuses are on (GMT-05:00) Eastern Time (US & Canada), not the Indiana East setting.
During the installation process, you will be prompted to enter information such as a name for your computer and an account name and password. This is for the computer's
administrator
account, and for security purposes should not be the account you will generally use (you can set up that account later). Keep this in mind as you choose a username and password you'll be able to remember.
Consider these descriptions to determine the best method for installing, reinstalling, or upgrading Windows, based on your needs and your manufacturer's recommendations:
In-place upgrade
Important notes:
UITS does
not
recommend this method, since in-place installations of operating systems tend to cause problems, especially if the new version is very different from the previous one; see
in-place upgrade
. For example, if you're doing a major version upgrade from
Windows 8
to
Windows 10
, then UITS generally recommends a clean installation instead.
If your operating system is corrupted or infected, an in-place upgrade will most likely retain this infection/corruption. In those cases, UITS strongly recommends installing via a Reset/Reset with the Remove everything option, Factory Recovery, or Clean installation.
Applies to:
Windows 7
and higher
What happens:
Installs a newer version of an operating system without removing the older version first (
Windows 8
to
Windows 10
,
Windows 10
Home to
Windows 10
Education, etc.); see
in-place upgrade
.
Generally, reinstalls Windows while preserving your programs, apps, files, and settings; however, only your personal files may be retained, depending on the version of Windows with which you begin and end (for example,
Windows 7
to
Windows 8.1
; see
Windows 8
and
Windows 8.1
Upgrade Paths
).
Additional notes:
While this option should preserve your files, UITS recommends backing up your files to be safe.
Currently installed programs may not be compatible with the upgraded operating system, and may not function at all. Be sure to check to see if you'll need a newer version of the program, and if one is available.
If you perform an in-place upgrade and have multiple, ongoing issues, then you will likely need to back up your files and perform a clean installation instead.
Refresh/Reset this PC with the Keep my files option
Warning:
If you're reinstalling due to an infection, UITS recommends installing via a Reset/Reset, Factory Recovery, or Clean installation instead, as this option may not remove the infection or all its effects.
Applies to:
Windows 8.1
and higher
(In
Windows 8.x
, this process is named "Refresh your PC", while in
Windows 10
, it is "Reset your PC with the Keep my files option".)
What happens:
Reinstalls Windows while preserving your files and personalization settings
Retains apps that came with your PC and that were installed from the Windows Store
Restores PC settings back to default
Removes installed desktop programs (such as Office)
Additional notes:
While this option should preserve your files, UITS recommends backing up your files to be safe.
A list of removed apps that you will need to reinstall is saved to your desktop.
Includes manufacturer-supplied drivers.
If refreshing the computer does not resolve your issues, try resetting it instead.
If you upgraded your PC from
Windows 8
to
Windows 8.1
and your PC has a
Windows 8
recovery partition, refreshing your PC will restore
Windows 8
. You'll need to upgrade to
Windows 8.1
via the Store app after the refresh has finished.
Refresh/Reset with the Remove everything option:
Applies to:
Windows 8.1
and higher
(In
Windows 8.x
, this process is named "Reset your PC". In
Windows 10
, this is "Reset your PC with the Remove everything option".)
What happens:
Reinstalls Windows back to factory settings via a hidden recovery partition.
Uses Microsoft Windows to perform the install.
Deletes files, settings, and applications you've installed (both Windows Store apps and desktop programs).
Retains apps and desktop programs that came with the device.
Additional notes:
Includes manufacturer-supplied drivers.
If you upgraded your PC from
Windows 8
to
Windows 8.1
and your PC has a
Windows 8
recovery partition, resetting your PC will restore
Windows 8
. You'll need to upgrade to
Windows 8.1
via the Store app after the reset has finished.
Factory Recovery:
Applies to:
Windows 7
and higher
What happens:
Reinstalls Windows back to factory settings via a hidden recovery partition.
Uses the computer manufacturer's software to perform the install.
Deletes files, settings, and applications you've installed (both Windows Store apps and desktop programs).
Retains apps and desktop programs that came with the device.
Additional notes:
Includes manufacturer-supplied drivers
Clean Install
Applies to:
Windows 7
and higher
What happens:
Installs Windows from installation media, such as a USB flash drive or DVD.
Deletes all files, settings, applications, and desktop programs (for example, Office).
Additional notes:
Warning about potential loss of drivers:
A clean installation of Windows includes Microsoft-supplied drivers, which may not be as up-to-date as those supplied by the manufacturer. As a result, some devices may not be detected, and you will need to get drivers from the manufacturer's site. If you are upgrading to a newer version of Windows (for example, from
Windows 7
to
Windows 8.1
), your computer manufacturer may not supply drivers for the new version of Windows, especially if your computer is several years old. Keep in mind that determining the correct drivers for your computer can be a tedious process of trial and error, even for the technically savvy. If you are reinstalling due to an infection, doing so by resetting or via a factory recovery process is both quicker and easier.
By the terms of the IU/Microsoft Campus Agreement, each license key for Windows obtained through IU is capable of installing the software on only one computer. If you need a second license, contact your campus

Also by the terms of the IU/Microsoft Campus Agreement, each license key for Windows obtained through IU can only be installed on a computer with an existing copy of Windows or via Boot Camp on a Mac.

This option is required if either of the following are applicable:

title: Use Helm charts to deploy and manage Kubernetes applications
content:
Table of contents
Overview
Install Helm
Set environment variables
Use charts
Add a chart repository
Chart values
Chart versions and upgrades
Maintain your own chart
Chart linting
GitHub status checks
Helm releases
Use the kube-deployer image
Use Harbor as a Helm repository
Roll back a deployment
Helm resources
Overview
Helm
is a command line tool that can help you deploy and manage your Kubernetes applications. A Helm chart contains a set of
Go templates
used to produce all of the Kubernetes manifests, such as Deployments, Services, Ingresses, and ConfigMaps, required to run applications. Helm renders these templates and can deploy, upgrade, and rollback your applications. Maintaining a Helm chart provides a consistent method of deploying applications that can be shared across teams. The following information will help you get started with Helm by using existing charts (or maintaining your own), as well as publishing and using charts in IU's Harbor registry.
Install Helm
To get started, you first need to
install Helm
. UITS suggests using the latest release of version 3. You also may use a pre-built Docker image containing the
helm
binary. UITS maintains
registry.docker.iu.edu/library/kube-deployer
, which is used for deploying applications to various IU Kubernetes clusters (for more, see
Configure delivery pipelines
). For information on using the
kube-deployer
image on your local machine, see the
Use the kube-deployer image
section below.
Set environment variables
There are several environment variables you can set to make working with Helm easier. For example,
HELM_NAMESPACE
lets you run
helm
without passing your Helm release namespace every time you perform an action:
export HELM_NAMESPACE="ua-vpit--enterprise-systems--esimw--helm-release"
For a complete list of environment variables, see Helm's
Environment Variables
page. For more about the Helm release namespace, see the
Helm releases
section below.
Use charts
You can create charts using the
helm create
command or by using a curated chart. For example, the
library/k8s-boot
chart is recommended for deploying Spring Boot applications on IU's enterprise Kubernetes environment.
Artifact Hub
(previously Helm Hub) is another repository with a variety of Helm charts.
For more on creating a chart, see Helm's
Getting Started
page.
For common Helm commands, see
Using Helm charts with the Enterprise Docker Registry (Harbor)
.
Add a chart repository
UITS maintains a
collection of public Docker images and Helm charts
in the production Harbor registry. Refer to the
Use Harbor as a Helm repository
section below for information on how to use OCI charts with Harbor.
For more, see the official
Helm Repo
documentation or run
helm repo --help
.
Chart values
Each chart contains a
values.yaml
file with some default values. You may override these values by creating a values file of your own and passing it to
helm
using the
--values
flag.
The values are replaced in the Go templates. To see the rendered templates, use the
helm template
command, or perform a dry run on an install or upgrade. Below are some sample commands for rendering the
k8s-boot
templates:
# Render library/k8s-boot templates using your custom values from `my-values.yaml`
helm template my-release oci://registry.docker.iu.edu/library/k8s-boot --values my-values.yaml
# Perform a dry run install (replace install with upgrade if you
# are upgrading to a new chart version)
helm install my-release oci://registry.docker.iu.edu/library/k8s-boot --values my-values.yaml --dry-run
For more, see the official
Values Files
documentation.
Chart versions and upgrades
To use a specific version of a chart, set the
--version
flag. For example, the
library/k8s-boot
latest version is 0.10.1, so the following could be used to upgrade an application deployment (note that this is the chart version, not your application version):
# Upgrade a release to chart version 0.10.1
helm upgrade my-release oci://registry.docker.iu.edu/library/k8s-boot --values my-values.yaml --version 0.10.1
If this is the first time you're deploying the application, use
helm install
. You also may add the
--install
flag to
helm upgrade
, which will install if no release exists.
For more, see the official
Helm Install
and
Helm Upgrade
pages.
Maintain your own chart
Chart linting
Helm provides a command for linting chart templates. To lint a chart, run the following:
helm lint
Check out
helm lint --help
for all the available flags.
GitHub status checks
GitHub provides an API for setting statuses on branches. By setting a status (for example, based on the outcome of
helm lint
), you can block a PR from being merged. There is a set of scripts in
this repository
to help facilitate GitHub status checks. There are also corresponding
Dockerfiles
for building an image that includes
helm
and the status check scripts. To create a plan in Bamboo for automatically linting and setting a status on your branch in Github, do the following:
Create a branch in your project that won't change (the contents are not important; for this example, it will be
bamboo
):
cd <chart repo>
git checkout --orphan bamboo
git rm -rf .                # leave the files not tracked by git
echo "bamboo" > index.html  # some content is required to commit and push
git add index.html
git ci -m "empty commit"
git push origin bamboo
Create a plan in Bamboo and open
Default plan configuration
.
Add your repository under "Repositories" and set "Branch" to
bamboo
.
Add a trigger under "Triggers" (for example,
Repository polling
.
Under "Branches" > "Create plan branch", you may choose to watch feature branches; for example, select
When new branch in repository is created and matches expression
and set regular expression to
feature/.+
.
Create a variable named
githubTokenSecret
and set the value to your GitHub API token.
Create a new stage and add a Helm Lint job.
On the
Docker
tab, set "Run this job in" to
Docker container
.
Set "Docker image" to
registry.docker.iu.edu/esimw/kube-github-status-check:stable
. (You may also use a specific
released version
tag, such as
1.1.1
).
On the
Tasks
tab, create the following tasks in this order:
Create a Source Code Checkout of your repository.
Create a Script task named
Set pending status on commit
.
Set "Script file" to
/usr/local/bin/mark-commit-pending
.
Set "Argument" to
--context="
Helm Linting
"
(or any description you like for the context flag).
Set "Environment variables" to
GITHUB_API_TOKEN="${bamboo.githubTokenSecret}"
.
Create a Script task named
Helm Lint
. Set the inline Script Body to
helm lint -f values.yaml --strict
.
Create a Script task named
Set success status on commit
.
Set "Script file" to
/usr/local/bin/mark-commit-successful
.
Set "Argument" to
--context="
Helm Linting
"
(or any description you like for the context flag).
Set "Environment variables" to
GITHUB_API_TOKEN="${bamboo.githubTokenSecret}"
.
Create a Script task named
Set failed status on commit if build failed
.
Set "Script file" to
/usr/local/bin/mark-commit-failed
.
Set "Argument" to
--context="
Helm Linting
"
(or any description you like for the context flag).
Set "Environment variables" to
GITHUB_API_TOKEN="${bamboo.githubTokenSecret}"
.
Save this task and drag it into the "Final tasks" section.
Helm releases
Helm stores its release information in a Kubernetes secret. By default, the last 10 revisions are kept, but you can override this by passing the
--history-max
flag to
helm install
and
helm upgrade
. For this reason, application manifests and Helm releases use different namespaces at IU. The convention at IU is to append
--helm-release
to your team's namespace; for example, if your team's namespace is
ua-vpit--enterprise-systems--esimw
, your Helm release namespace would be
ua-vpit--enterprise-systems--esimw--helm-release
. This allows Helm to manage its secrets while keeping secrets in the team's namespace secure.
You will need to pass this namespace on every
helm
command that interacts with a Kubernetes cluster. For example:
helm install my-release stable/chart -n ua-vpit--enterprise-systems--esimw--helm-release
helm list -n ua-vpit--enterprise-systems--esimw--helm-release
Use the kube-deployer image
The
Configure delivery pipelines
page contains information on deploying applications using an environment like Bamboo, but you may also use it locally if you don't have Helm installed and want to execute Helm commands in a Docker container.
To check the version of
helm
installed, use:
docker run --rm registry.docker.iu.edu/library/kube-deployer:1.0.0 bash -c '
helm version
'
Here is an example of rendering the default
bitnami/node
templates to STDOUT using the default values and latest version of the chart:
docker run --rm \
registry.docker.iu.edu/library/kube-deployer:1.0.0 bash -c '
helm repo add bitnami https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
helm repo update
helm template my-release bitnami/node
'
If you are developing a custom chart not found in a Helm repository, you can mount the source into the container. This result can be achieved in one of two ways:
Create a new Dockerfile FROM kube-deployer:
By default,
kube-deployer
's deploy script will look inside the
/helm
directory for a chart to use when deploying. Therefore, you can build your own image and copy your packaged Helm chart into the
/helm
directory:
FROM registry.docker.iu.edu/library/kube-deployer:
<most recent version of kube-deployer>
# We want to ADD this file instead of COPYing so it automatically extracts it
ADD my-chart-*.tgz /
RUN mv /my-chart /helm
From your chart's working directory:
helm package .
docker build .
Mount the chart into a container:
This command will render your custom chart templates to STDOUT. It assumes your chart is checked out on your local machine at
/path/to/your/chart
and your application source is at
/path/to/your/project
. It also assumes your custom values file is in that project directory and named
your-project-values.yaml
. Your chart is mounted at
/chart
inside the container and your project at
/project
. This command also sets your container working directory to your project directory
/project
. Replace these values as necessary.
docker run --rm \
-v
/path/to/your/chart
:/chart \
-v
/path/to/your/project
:/project \
-w /project
registry.docker.iu.edu/library/kube-deployer:1.0.0 bash -c '
helm template my-release /chart --values
your-project-values.yaml
'
To interact with a Kubernetes cluster, you need to mount your Kubernetes configuration file; for example, the following command will mount your Kubernetes configuration file and list your Helm releases (replace
your-helm-release-namespace
with your Kubernetes namespace; see
Connect to IU's Enterprise Kubernetes Environment
for more information if you don't have a config file.
docker run --rm \
-v $HOME/.kube/config:/root/.kube/config \
registry.docker.iu.edu/library/kube-deployer:stable bash -c '
helm list -n your-helm-release-namespace
'
Use Harbor as a Helm repository
Harbor
provides OCI-compliant storage for your Helm charts. Below are instructions for packaging and uploading your charts to Harbor using the OCI format.
Update
Chart.yaml
and set the
version
property. Below is an example
Chart.yaml
apiVersion: v2
name: my-chart
description: A sample chart
type: application
version: 1.0.0
Package your chart.
cd
/path/to/your/my-chart
helm package .
This produces a tarball named
my-chart-1.0.0.tgz
.
Authenticate with Harbor using the
registry login
command (see
Get credentials for your CI process and CLI usage
).
echo "
<password>
" | helm registry login registry.docker.iu.edu -u
<username>
--password-stdin
Push your packaged chart to Harbor using the OCI format. Replace
<project>
with your Harbor project name (for example,
esimw
).
helm push my-chart-1.0.0.tgz oci://registry.docker.iu.edu/
<project>
Pull charts from Harbor using the OCI format.
# Pull a specific version of a chart
helm pull oci://registry.docker.iu.edu/<project>/my-chart --version 1.0.0
Deploy using OCI charts. Below are sample commands showing how to work with your OCI charts in Harbor:
# Install a release directly from the OCI registry
helm install my-release oci://registry.docker.iu.edu/<project>/my-chart --version 1.0.0
# Upgrade a release using OCI format
helm upgrade my-release oci://registry.docker.iu.edu/<project>/my-chart --version 1.0.0
# Render Helm templates from OCI registry
helm template my-release oci://registry.docker.iu.edu/<project>/my-chart --version 1.0.0
# Show chart information from OCI registry
helm show chart oci://registry.docker.iu.edu/<project>/my-chart --version 1.0.0
Note:
Harbor no longer uses Chart Museum. Charts are now stored using the OCI format as described above.
Roll back a deployment
To roll back a release, use the
helm rollback
command. Make sure you have
exported the
HELM_NAMESPACE
variable
.
To see the history of releases, use
helm history
:
helm history <app>-<env>
Example output:
REVISION	UPDATED                 	STATUS    	CHART          	APP VERSION	DESCRIPTION
116     	Thu Apr 20 19:00:19 2023	superseded	k8s-boot-3.11.0	           	Upgrade complete
117     	Wed Apr 26 20:01:14 2023	superseded	k8s-boot-3.11.0	           	Upgrade complete
118     	Thu Apr 27 15:29:50 2023	deployed  	k8s-boot-3.11.0	           	Upgrade complete
You can now run
helm-rollback <app>-<env>
to roll back the previous version (117 from 118 above) or
helm rollback <app>-<env> <revision>
to roll back to a specific revision.
Example output:
REVISION	UPDATED                 	STATUS    	CHART          	APP VERSION	DESCRIPTION
116     	Thu Apr 20 19:00:19 2023	superseded	k8s-boot-3.11.0	           	Upgrade complete
117     	Wed Apr 26 20:01:14 2023	superseded	k8s-boot-3.11.0	           	Upgrade complete
118     	Thu Apr 27 15:29:50 2023	superseded	k8s-boot-3.11.0	           	Upgrade complete
119     	Fri Apr 28 10:18:10 2023	deployed  	k8s-boot-3.11.0	           	Rollback to 117

Helm Docs Home
Quickstart Guide
Charts
Chart Best Practices Guide
Chart Template Developer's Guide
Helm Cheat Sheet
Frequently Asked Questions

At Indiana University, on the Enterprise System (ES) nodes, the modules that come with the default Perl installation are listed in the perlmodlib perldoc. To access it, enter the following command:
perldoc perlmodlib

perldoc perllocal
To check for a specific module (for example,

perl -MCGI -e "CGI.pm"
If no errors are returned, the module was found successfully. If the module was not found, to request that it be added, see
Request new software on the IU ES nodes
.

perl -MNet::SSLeay -e "print Net::SSLeay->VERSION"

title: Use external modules and other advanced functionality in IU REDCap
content:
Table of contents
Overview
REDCap API
Access from Tableau
External modules
REDCap-ETL
API Sync, Copy Data on Save, and Cross-Project Piping
Flight Tracker
Other external modules available in IU REDCap
Request more external modules
Get help
Overview
IU REDCap
users can use the
Advanced Functionality Request
form to request access to certain advanced functionality, third-party external modules,
REDCap-ETL
(
REDCap
Extract, Transform, Load) and/or the
REDCap API
. The form aims to reduce the risk of security, privacy, and performance issues by warning you of possible concerns and providing guidance on how to avoid them.
Note:
External modules are add-on packages of software that can extend REDCap's current functionality, as well as provide customizations and enhancements for REDCap's existing behavior and appearance, either at the system level or project level. While IU REDCap vets third-party external modules for security and privacy, it does not maintain them.
Use them at your own risk.
REDCap-ETL is not a third-party external module; it is developed and maintained by IU REDCap.
Some third-party external modules are available within your IU REDCap project without needing any additional approval, so they are not listed in the
Advanced Functionality Request
form. Other third-party external modules could potentially be made available within IU REDCap, but doing so may require a lengthy vetting process.
Important:
If the IU
REDCap
project data you are accessing contain protected health information (
PHI
), you must treat the data as PHI, which means files must be encrypted when they are stored (at rest) and when they are transferred from one system to another (in transit). For more, see:
Recommended tools for encrypting data containing HIPAA-regulated PHI
Your legal responsibilities for protecting data containing protected health information (PHI) when using UITS Research Technologies systems and services
If you have questions about securing HIPAA-regulated research data at IU, email
securemyresearch@iu.edu
.
SecureMyResearch
provides self-service resources and one-on-one consulting to help IU researchers, faculty, and staff meet cybersecurity and compliance requirements for processing, storing, and sharing regulated and unregulated research data; for more, see
About SecureMyResearch
. To learn more about properly ensuring the safe handling of
PHI
on UITS systems, see the UITS IT Training video
Securing HIPAA Workflows on UITS Systems
. To learn about division of responsibilities for securing PHI, see
Shared responsibility model for securing PHI on UITS systems
.
REDCap API
You can use the
Advanced Functionality Request
form to request access to the REDCap API if you are planning to use Tableau, create a custom API software client, or use an external module that requires the API (such as REDCap-ETL or API Sync).
The REDCap API (Application Programming Interface) is used to programmatically import/export data. See
Get started with the REDCap API
.
Access from Tableau
You can use the
Advanced Functionality Request
form to request access to IU REDCap from Tableau. The retrieval of data from IU REDCap into Tableau also requires REDCap API access. See
Use your IU REDCap project as a data source in Tableau
.
External modules
You can use the
Advanced Functionality Request
form to request that the following external modules be enabled in your REDCap project(s).
REDCap-ETL
REDCap-ETL automates the transformation and export of data into relational form for use in relational databases, such as MySQL, SQL Server, and PostgreSQL. A REDCap API token is required. For more, see
Use REDCap-ETL to transform and move data from IU REDCap to another service
.
API Sync, Copy Data on Save, and Cross-Project Piping
API Sync:
The API Sync external module transfers data between projects. Data transfers can be scheduled or manual. A REDCap API token is required. API Sync automates exporting/importing to/from REDCap servers via the API. The Data Dictionaries for the local and remote projects are expected to be either identical or compatible.
Copy Data on Save:
The Copy Data on Save external module transfers data to other REDCap projects. Data transfers are triggered by new data. Copy Data on Save copies data from one place to another when you save a form. You can set up multiple copy processes to different projects or to other fields in the same project.
Cross-Project Piping:
The Cross-Project Piping external module pulls data from other projects. Data pulls are performed manually or triggered by saves. Cross-Project Piping "pipes" from one field in one project into another field in another project during data entry (not surveys). The projects have to be matched on a third field in both projects. Enable this module in the destination project, and select appropriate fields in the configure panel.
Flight Tracker
The Flight Tracker external module tracks scholarly career development. Flight Tracker tracks a scholarly group's career development by charting publications, grants, and patents over time. Training grants and other scholar communities can benefit from graphical, analytical, and reporting tools, including automatically produced drafts of NIH training tables. Only US data are supported.
Other external modules available in IU REDCap
The following third-party external modules are available within your IU REDCap project without any additional approval, so they are not listed in the
Advanced Functionality Request
form. These external modules can be enabled by selecting
Manage
in the "External Modules" section on the left side of the REDCap project page and then selecting
Enable a Module
.
Auto-Record Generation:
This module allows for a new record to be generated in another project (or the same project) on a flagging field being saved, and allows for data fields to be transferred to the new record, as well. Events and repeating instruments are not currently supported.
Date Calculated Fields:
This module allows for "piping" (automatically copying) from date fields to other date fields, regardless of format. It can pipe data across events within a REDCap project.
Geomarker:
Geomarker generates a Google map with marker and information windows using geolocation data from specified fields in a REDCap project.
HIDESUBMIT Action Tags:
This module allows users to conditionally hide various Submit/Save/Next instance buttons on surveys and/or data entry forms using action tags and branching logic.
Image Map:
This module replaces an input, radio, or checkbox field with an interactive image where users can click on image regions to select one or more field options. For complete documentation and an example instrument, see
https://github.com/ctsit/imagemap
.
Instance Table:
Use the action tag
@INSTANCETABLE=form_name
in a descriptive text field to include a table showing data from repeat instances of that form. If your project is longitudinal, use
@INSTANCETABLE=event_name:form_name
to specify the event and form (a repeating form or a form in a repeating event). Other action tags are available for controlling certain properties of the tables and their contents.
Matrix Question Randomization:
This module randomizes the order of the questions for specified matrices on survey pages and highlights rows in red that were missed on the first form submission.
No Copy/Paste:
This module prevents copying from or pasting into fields.
Rename File Upload:
Tag file fields with the action tag
@RENAME-UPLOAD='name_pattern'
to specify how files uploaded to the field should be renamed; piping of fields and smart variables into the file name is supported. Examples:
@RENAME-UPLOAD='MyCustomFilenamePattern_rec-[record-name]'
@RENAME-UPLOAD='MyCustomFilenamePattern_[project-id]-[record-name]-[filename_part]'
@RENAME-UPLOAD='MyCustomFilenamePattern_[record-name]-[survey-time-completed]'
Do not include any file extension within the pattern. Renamed files will keep the extension with which they were uploaded. For suggestions on characters to avoid in filenames, see
Problematic characters
.
Request more external modules
Other third-party external modules may potentially be made available within IU REDCap, but doing so may require a lengthy vetting process. To learn what is available, see the
REDCapRepo
. To request vetting of an external module, email
redcap@iu.edu
specifying the module of interest and how it will help meet your needs.
Get help
If you have questions about the
Advanced Functionality Request
form or external modules in IU REDCap, email IU REDCap Support at
redcap@iu.edu
.

title: Use REDCap-ETL to transform and move data from IU REDCap to another service
content:
Table of contents
Overview
Run
REDCap
-ETL
within IU
REDCap
Run
REDCap
-ETL
as standalone software
Get started
Overview
REDCap
-ETL
(
REDCap
Extract, Transform, Load) extracts data from
REDCap
, transforms it into a relational format, and loads that data to a relational database or, if run as standalone software, to an SQLite file or a series of CSV files.
REDCap
-ETL
can be run within
IU
REDCap
or as standalone software.
Important:
If the IU
REDCap
project data you are accessing contain protected health information (
PHI
), you must treat the data as PHI, which means files must be encrypted when they are stored (at rest) and when they are transferred from one system to another (in transit). For more, see:
Recommended tools for encrypting data containing HIPAA-regulated PHI
Your legal responsibilities for protecting data containing protected health information (PHI) when using UITS Research Technologies systems and services
If you have questions about securing HIPAA-regulated research data at IU, email
securemyresearch@iu.edu
.
SecureMyResearch
provides self-service resources and one-on-one consulting to help IU researchers, faculty, and staff meet cybersecurity and compliance requirements for processing, storing, and sharing regulated and unregulated research data; for more, see
About SecureMyResearch
. To learn more about properly ensuring the safe handling of
PHI
on UITS systems, see the UITS IT Training video
Securing HIPAA Workflows on UITS Systems
. To learn about division of responsibilities for securing PHI, see
Shared responsibility model for securing PHI on UITS systems
.
Run
REDCap
-ETL
within IU
REDCap
A
REDCap
-ETL
interface is available within IU
REDCap
as an external module. The
REDCap
-ETL
external module provides a graphical interface for configuring
REDCap
-ETL
, enables
REDCap
-ETL
to be scheduled, and can generate at the press of a button the transformation rules needed by
REDCap
-ETL
to define how to transform
REDCap
data into a relational format.
The
REDCap
-ETL
external module allows data to be loaded into relational databases such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server, and to be downloaded interactively as a set of CSV files. When downloading CSV files, the
REDCap
-ETL
external module cannot be scheduled.
For more about the
REDCap
-ETL
external module, see
REDCap
-ETL
External Module
.
Run
REDCap
-ETL
as standalone software
REDCap
-ETL
can be run as standalone software. Doing so requires a server to host
REDCap
-ETL
. The
REDCap
-ETL
configuration, including the transformation rules that define how to transform
REDCap

REDCap

title: What to do before you contact the UITS Support Center for help
content:

Check the Knowledge Base first
UITS
Support Center consultants initiate a great deal of Knowledge Base content in response to questions people in the IU community ask. Searching this Knowledge Base for help with your problem before calling or emailing the Support Center may give you a speedier answer (enter your search terms in the box at the top of this page).
Contact the Support Center
If the Knowledge Base does not address your problem or if you need further assistance, contact your
campus Support Center
. Provide as much of the following information as possible. If you call, have the information available, be at your computer, and have the computer turned on.
What operating system are you using (for example,
Windows 11
, macOS 10.12)?
If the problem has to do with software, what version of that software are you using (for example, Microsoft Outlook 2016)?
It often helps to provide some context, for example:
What you were trying to do
Whether you've ever been able to do this, and if so, if anything about your system has changed since then
If you've done anything to try to fix the problem
How long the problem has been occurring
If you received an error message, note its exact text. Some error messages have a
Details
button. Click the
Details
button, if available, to show a more complete error similar to this:
"
programname.exe
caused an invalid page fault / general protection fault in module XXXXX at xxxx:xxxxxxxx"
This is followed by a list of numbers called the register dump. Copy the complete error message for the Support Center, but ignore the long register dump.
Get help for new computer hardware or software
If your computer is less than a year old and you have problems with its DVD drive, wireless card, network card, monitor, or any other hardware or software that came with the computer, contact the computer vendor. A technical support phone number should be available in the computer's user manual. For new computers, free technical support and warranty coverage are usually available for a limited time (usually one year). If you were sold a computer with faulty components, contact the vendor right away.
If you have problems with the software you purchased for your computer, contact the technical support number for that software package before contacting the Support Center. Software companies often provide either 30 to 90 days worth of free support, or free help for the first one or two questions.

title: Honorlock for IU students
content:
Table of contents
Overview
Cost of Honorlock
Technology requirements
Prepare for a proctored assessment
Before your first assessment with Honorlock
Before every assessment with Honorlock
Launch and take an assessment with Honorlock
Canvas Quizzes
Third-party assessments
Learn more
Get help
Overview
Honorlock is an online proctoring service that allows online and distance learners to take exams without needing to schedule an on-campus visit or proctor. Honorlock uses a combination of AI and live human proctors to monitor your exam. The AI scans for unusual activity, such as unexpected movement or someone entering the room, and flags potential concerns. If a flag is triggered, a live proctor will check the exam session. They may briefly pause your exam and open a chat with you, offering assistance in returning to your exam. Once the exam is complete, your instructor has access to the recordings and any flags, and can review them.
For more about Honorlock's privacy policies, see:
Student Privacy Statement
Honorlock Privacy Policy
Cost of Honorlock
The costs for using Honorlock are covered by IU Online or the school or department offering the course.  You should never be charged for the use of Honorlock in your Indiana University courses.
Technology requirements
In order to take an assessment that uses Honorlock, you will need:
A computer running Windows 10 or 11, macOS 10.14 or higher, or ChromeOS (Chromebooks)
The Google Chrome browser version 120 or higher with the
Honorlock Chrome Extension
enabled
A built-in or external webcam and microphone
An internet connection rated at 1.5 Mbps download/750 Kbps upload. To test your internet speed, visit
http://www.speedtest.net
.
Dual monitors are not permitted. If the software detects more than one monitor, see
Multiple Monitors Detected
.
Notes:
For the most up-to-date requirements information, see
Minimum System Requirements
.
Currently, Honorlock is incompatible with:
Tablets and mobile devices
Walmart-branded cameras (Onn/Surf Onn)
Amcrest cameras
Nexigo cameras
Prepare for a proctored assessment
Before your first assessment with Honorlock
Install
the Honorlock extension for the Chrome browser
. This will save setup time before the exam. For step-by-step instructions, see
Install the Honorlock Extension
.
Watch the following videos to see what to expect before the exam starts and during the the exam:
Honorlock Best Practices
Proctoring Overview
Student Guide: How to Use Honorlock
Your experience with Honorlock may be slightly different than what’s shown in the videos because your instructor may have chosen different proctoring settings.
Before every assessment with Honorlock
Before you start an assessment with Honorlock, take the following steps to ensure you, your equipment, and your test-taking environment meet the requirements of the assessment and the Honorlock software.
Make sure your test-taking equipment meets the
Honorlock minimum system requirements
and the Honorlock extension has been added to Chrome.
Try to use the bathroom before you start the assessment.  You may not be permitted to leave the room after it starts.
Find a well-lit room with a door to take the test so there are no interruptions during the assessment. Ideally, the room should be equipped with a desk (or table) and chair so you can sit upright while taking the exam.
Place your official student ID on the table (or desk) so you can locate it easily when prompted to take a photo of it.
If your instructor provides the assessment guidelines beforehand, remove all disallowed equipment and materials from the room.  Otherwise, review the test-taker guidelines when you start the assessment and make adjustments to bring your environment into compliance.
Make sure your face is visible on the webcam throughout the exam.
Launch and take an assessment with Honorlock
Important:
When you launch a proctored assessment, the Honorlock software will walk you through a series of pre-assessment checks before the assessment begins. Read the on-screen prompts carefully and follow the instructions.
You may be asked to perform an ID verification. Honorlock will prompt you to take a picture of an official ID (such as your CrimsonCard, driver's license, state ID, etc). During this process, the name on your ID will be compared to your name in Canvas (which uses your
preferred name
in the Student Center). They don't need to match exactly, but if there are significant differences, you'll be asked to try again. If you're unable to pass the ID verification after three tries, select the
Contact Support
button at the bottom of the "ID Verification" screen.
Honorlock will show you the test-taker guidelines selected by your instructor, which will tell you the behaviors and resources that are allowed and disallowed. Read them carefully and make sure you remain compliant throughout the exam.
If you encounter any problems during the assessment, select the chat icon at the lower right to contact Honorlock support. If you are unable to start the in-app chat, open a separate browser tab, go to
https://honorlock.com/support
, and select
Begin Live Chat
.
You should never need to enter the password for an assessment. When the exam password is requested, Honorlock will enter it for you.
The timer for the assessment will not begin until after the password has been entered and the first question in the assessment is displayed.
Canvas Quizzes
Honorlock is fully integrated with Canvas and Canvas Quizzes. If your instructor provided specific instructions on where to find and take your quiz, follow those instructions. Otherwise, for quizzes created in Canvas, you can navigate to the quiz wherever it is located in your course (Quizzes, Assignments, Modules, etc.) and select the title of the quiz to get started. All of your proctored quizzes will also be listed in the Honorlock tool (located in the course navigation). You can launch them from there as well.
For step-by-step instructions, see
How to Use Honorlock (Test Takers
). If your experience doesn't match the Honorlock guide exactly, don't worry. Depending on the proctoring settings selected by your instructor, some of the steps may not apply to you.
Third-party assessments
Honorlock can also be used to proctor assessments created outside of Canvas, such as in a publisher courseware site. To start a third-party assessment:
Open the Honorlock tool and locate the assessment on the main Honorlock screen. Even if there's a link to the assessment elsewhere in your course, you must launch the assessment from within the Honorlock tool.
To start the assessment, choose
Launch
, and follow the on-screen instructions.
After completing the pre-assessment checks, Honorlock will prompt you to open the assessment in a new tab. It may not always be possible to deliver you directly to the assessment. If you are taken to the main page of the third-party tool, you'll need to navigate to the assessment on your own.
Once you reach the password prompt for the assessment, in the Honorlock window at the lower left, select
I have found my assessment
. Then select
Unlock assessment
. Honorlock will enter the password for you so you can begin the exam.
For more in-depth instructions, see
How to Use Honorlock with a Universal Exam (Test Takers)
. If your experience doesn't match the Honorlock guide exactly, don't worry. Depending on the proctoring settings selected by your instructor, some of the steps may not apply to you.
Learn more
Consult the following Honorlock resources for students:
Test Taker Resources
(all Honorlock Guides for Students)
Launching Honorlock from Your Exam
Completing a Room Scan Using Honorlock
Honorlock FAQs for Test Takers
Honorlock Toolbar Overview for Test Takers
Honorlock Best Practices for Test Takers
Student Privacy Statement

Student Privacy FAQ
Get help
For live assistance from a proctor, use the in-app chat tool, or go to
https://honorlock.com/support
and select
Begin Live Chat
.
For less urgent assistance, send an email message to
support@honorlock.com
.

title: Improve and troubleshoot your Zoom experience
content:
Table of contents
Overview
Improve your experience
Review technical requirements
Check your network
Adjust your computer's settings
Adjust Zoom settings
Troubleshoot
I can't join my meeting
I've joined my meeting, but no one else is here
I can't hear or talk to people
I want to turn off Zoom's automatic audio adjustments
People can't see me
My video is poor quality
I can't screenshare a video with sound
I can't access my recordings, I accidentally deleted a recording, or I can't record
My recording won't convert

My problem isn't listed here
Overview
Important:
Due to federal law enforcement concerns regarding foreign government interference and surveillance risks associated with Zoom, it is strongly recommended that individuals involved in research activities discontinue using Zoom. Instead, all virtual meetings should be conducted through
Microsoft Teams
, which meets government requirements for secure and private communications.
IU Research has chosen to prohibit the use of Zoom by its employees. Other IU divisions may enact similar prohibitions.
To learn more about using Microsoft Teams for virtual meetings, see
UITS IT Training Microsoft resources
.
For questions or further guidance,
contact your local UITS Support Center
.
If Zoom appears to distort audio or video, or does not perform in a manner you expect, use the information here to improve your experience, or troubleshoot issues.
Improve your experience
Review technical requirements
Review
Zoom's system requirements
and ensure your system meets these recommendations.
Check your network
Check your network speeds using one of the free services available online. Zoom's system requirements recommend a minimum of 1.5 Mbps for both upload and download speed. If necessary, check with your internet service provider.
Power cycle your modem/router, if possible.
If you're on a wireless connection:
Confirm that you have a strong signal.
Connect to a 5 GHz network (rather than 2.4 GHz), if possible.
Limit the number of devices connected to your wireless router.
Consider switching to a wired connection.
Ensure that other devices on your network aren't consuming bandwidth; these could include cloud-connected security cameras, cloud backup solutions, smart TVs, streaming devices, smart hubs, gaming devices, or other cloud or internet-connected devices. You can turn them off, lower the bandwidth they consume by adjusting performance settings, or make other changes that may improve the amount of bandwidth available for Zoom.
If you're using a network-wide VPN, consider disabling it.
Important:
Do not disable any necessary devices that help protect or otherwise secure your network.
If you can't improve or resolve your connection, check with your internet service provider.
Adjust your computer's settings
Restart your Zoom client.
Restart your computer.
Update system drivers, especially network drivers, if necessary.
Close out of any unneeded programs, especially those that use the internet. This could include office applications, additional browser tabs, or anything that uses system or network resources. Closing out of these items will free more system resources for Zoom to use.
Stop all downloads, uploads, or other unnecessary processes that are using network resources.
Ensure that your devices are up to date.
Ensure that your application(s) are up to date, especially the Zoom client.
Disconnect from any VPNs you may be using.
Adjust Zoom settings
Disable HD Video from your Zoom client:
While not in a call, select the
Home
tab.
Select the gear icon (
Settings
).
In the left Navigation pane, select
Video
.
Uncheck
Enable HD
.
Select
X
in the top right corner to close the Settings window.
Disable "Touch up my appearance" from your Zoom client:
While not in a call, select the
Home
tab.
Select the gear icon (
Settings
).
In the left Navigation pane, select
Video
.
Deselect
Touch up my appearance
.
Select the
X
in the top right corner to close the Settings window.
Mute your audio when not speaking.
Consider disabling your webcam if it's not necessary.
Troubleshoot
I can't join my meeting
If you're unable to join a meeting, check these items:
If you're on a desktop or mobile device, be sure you've
installed the Zoom client
and that it's up to date; see
Viewing the Zoom version number
If you've received any of these messages:
You are on hold:
The host has enabled a waiting room; you'll remain on hold until the host admits you into the meeting room.
Room connector is not enabled for this meeting:
If you are using videoconferencing equipment to join a meeting hosted by a free Zoom account or an account that doesn't have the room connector enabled, you will receive this error. Connect to the meeting using a desktop or mobile device instead.
Please wait for the host to start this meeting:
The
Join before host
feature is not enabled, and the host has not yet joined the meeting. Hosts automatically receive email asking them to join. You will be prompted to join the meeting a short time after the host joins.
Please enter the meeting password:
The meeting requires a passcode; enter the passcode provided by the meeting host (in the Zoom meeting invitation). If you do not know the passcode, contact the meeting host for assistance.
Note:
If you are connecting via telephone, and the IU Zoom meeting passcode contains alphabetic characters, check the meeting invitation for an all-numeric passcode (which Zoom generates automatically when the host sets a passcode containing alphabetic characters).
This meeting does not allow phone dial-in:
The host may only have allowed VoIP audio. In this case, if you dial into the general Zoom teleconferencing number and enter the meeting ID, you will hear the message above and the call will disconnect. You will need to
join the meeting
with a computer or a smartphone app.
Not meeting host. (3,003):
If you received a link to a Zoom meeting in the format
http://iu.zoom.us/meeting/123456789
, change
/meeting/
in the URL to
/j/
and try to connect again. For example,
http://iu.zoom.us/meeting/123456789
should instead be
http://iu.zoom.us/j/123456789
.
I've joined my meeting, but no one else is here
If you've joined a meeting but don't see other participants:
Confirm with the meeting host that the meeting has begun. If it has, ask for the meeting ID at the top of the host's Zoom window (for example, Zoom Meeting ID: 123-456-7890) and compare that to the meeting ID at the top of yours. If they don't match, you've joined a different meeting. Ask the host for the meeting ID, and
join that meeting
.
If you're the host, check whether the
waiting room is enabled
. If it is, you may need to manually admit your participants before they can join your meeting.
I can't hear or talk to people
If you're unable to hear or talk to people in a meeting:
Check the attendee controls at the bottom of your meeting window. If you see the Join Audio icon
on the far left, select it. (If you've already joined your audio, you'll instead see the mute/unmute icon
.)
To check whether the issue is related to the Zoom program, see:
Testing computer or device audio
My audio is not working on iOS or Android
Audio settings for iOS
(iPhone, iPad)
If your audio isn't working in the Zoom client
outside of the meeting
, try troubleshooting the device itself. For instructions, see
Troubleshoot audio and video issues on your computer or mobile device
.
The host may have allowed only telephony audio. In this case, you will not see the message "join meeting with computer audio". You may still be able to join the meeting with video or
via phone
.
I want to turn off Zoom's automatic audio adjustments
For musical content, applied lessons, or other situations where preserving audio quality is important, you can change Zoom's audio settings to minimize automatic adjustments such as gain, extended frequency response, and echo cancellation.
While turning off automatic adjustments can preserve the natural sounds of music, singing, or spoken word, it also requires meeting participants to position their microphones and speakers properly, and to manually adjust their microphone levels. Good conferencing etiquette is also important with these settings; participants should use headphones when possible and mute their microphones when not speaking or playing.
Note:
Network connection also impacts audio quality. Consider disabling video for a better audio experience.
These are advanced features; the instructions below assume you have basic knowledge of Zoom and your computer's audio and video settings.
To turn off automatic audio adjustments:
Log into
Zoom
.
Select
Settings
from the menu at the top or left side of the page.
Under "In Meeting (advanced)", make sure these settings are toggled on (blue):
Allow users to select stereo audio in their client settings
Allow users to select original sound in their client settings
Launch your meeting normally.
Each
meeting host and participant must then:
From the Zoom client, select the gear icon (
) in the upper right.
Select
Audio
from the menu on the left.
Under the microphone settings, uncheck
Automatically adjust volume
.
Select
Advanced
in the lower right.
Check
Show in-meeting option to "Enable Original Sound" from microphone
.
From the drop-down menus under "Audio Processing", set "Suppress Persistent Background Noise" and "Suppress Intermittent Background Noise" to
Disable
.
Close the settings window.
At the top of the meeting window, a
Turn [on/off] Original Sound
button will now be visible. Turn original sound on to transmit more natural audio to other participants. Turn it off to restore default settings.
Remember that
each
participant will need to adjust their settings to transmit natural sound. Be prepared to advise other participants on how to adjust their audio settings and speaker and microphone placement for best results.
People can't see me
If you've joined a meeting successfully but others can't see you:
Make sure your video isn't turned off by checking the Start Video icon
in the attendee controls at the bottom of your meeting window.
If you're connecting from a Lenovo device and your video isn't working, see
Video not working on Lenovo devices
.
If your video isn't working in the Zoom client
outside of the meeting
, try troubleshooting the device itself. For instructions, see
Troubleshoot audio and video issues on your computer or mobile device
.
My video is poor quality
The "Optimize for full screen video clip" setting greatly reduces video quality. Restart the screen share with that setting unchecked.
If you are experiencing a problem with the internet or the device itself, see
Troubleshoot audio and video issues on your computer or mobile device
.
I can't screenshare a video with sound
Make sure you've muted unneeded microphones (your device and/or the Zoom meeting microphone). After you select
Share
to share your screen, select
Share computer sound
in the lower left of the screenshare window.
I can't access my recordings, I accidentally deleted a recording, or I can't record
If your meeting is missing from the recorded meetings list in the Zoom client (for example, as a result of pressing
Delete
in the Zoom client for a recorded meeting), you may be able to find the recording on your device in its Zoom recordings folder.
To see where your Zoom recordings are stored, see the "Change location for Recording" section of
Local recording
. Recordings will be named in the format
double_click_to_convert_01.zoom
. When you find the
.zoom
file you are looking for, double-click it.
Note:
Pressing
Delete
in the Zoom client removes the recording from the recorded meetings list in Zoom, but not from the device itself.
Only current hosts can record a meeting. If you can't record, check to see whether you're the host by selecting the Participants icon
in the attendee controls at the bottom of your meeting window; if you aren't the host, you can ask the host to record the meeting.
For more about recording Zoom meetings, see
Create and store recordings of Zoom meetings
.
My recording won't convert
Your device might be low on disk space. To check, see:
Windows 11
and
Windows 10
:
Find out how much storage your PC has
Windows 8.x:
Tips to free up drive space on your PC
macOS:
How to free up storage space on your Mac
Error adding alternative hosts
To add an alternative host, you must enter that person's full
@iu.edu
email address, even if the person's primary email address uses another domain. Zoom recognizes
@iu.edu
email addresses only.
The desired host must have logged into Zoom at least once before you can add that person to any meeting.
People from outside IU cannot be added as hosts. This includes people with free or individual accounts, or accounts from other institutions.

contact UITS Learning Spaces Support
.

title: Effects of third-party cookies in Canvas
content:
Table of contents
Changes to Chrome
If you suspect third-party cookies are causing an error
Temporary fix for instructors
More about cookies
How browsers use cookies
About third-party (or "cross-domain") cookies
How browsers handle third-party cookies
Changes to Chrome
In February 2020, Google released version 80 of its Chrome web browser, which changes the way third-party cookies are handled. By default, Chrome will block third-party cookies unless the embedded web application takes necessary steps to prevent the cookies from being blocked.
In Canvas, you may experience difficulties launching third-party tools from the course navigation menu, course modules, and elsewhere while UITS works with application providers to patch their software to comply with Chrome 80.
Note:
Do not alter your web browser's settings to force your browser to accept third-party cookies, as they can pose risks to privacy and/or security. UITS recommends that you leave your browser's default cookie settings in place.
If you suspect third-party cookies are causing an error
Try a different web browser:
This is often the quickest troubleshooting step to try. If you have another browser (or two), try opening the problematic page in a different web browser to see if it functions properly.
Visit the embedded tool directly to establish "first party trust" with it:
If you know the website URL for the embedded service that you suspect is failing due to a blocked third-party cookie, try visiting that website in its own browser tab. This may establish what's called "first party trust" with the external application, allowing the embedded application to then function properly in Canvas.
Contact the Support Center:
Your campus
Support Center
may be able to help you troubleshoot the issue and determine if third-party cookies are in fact the problem.
Report the problem to your instructor:
If you experience problems loading external tools in Canvas, alert your instructor. It may be possible to provide access to the external tool/resource in a way that does not involve third-party cookies.
Temporary fix for instructors
If a third-party tool is broken in your course site due to a third-party cookie issue, try this workaround:
Create a new module in your course site called "Canvas Third-party Tools" or another name you choose. (If you aren't sure how to use Canvas Modules, see the Modules section of the
Canvas Guides
).
In the new module, click
+
(Add Item) to add a new item to the module.
From the
Add
drop-down menu in the "Add Item" window, select
External Tool
.
Select the desired tool from the external tools list. Scroll to the bottom of the window and check
Load in a new tab
. Loading the tool in a new tab will circumvent the third-party cookies problem. If you wish, you can also change the display name of the tool by editing the Page Name.
To finish adding the tool to the module, click
Add Item
.
Repeat steps 1-5 for each problem tool.
Publish the module and items. Your students will now be able to launch the tools from Canvas Modules.
If you receive an "Access Denied" message:
Make sure you're running the most recent version of Chrome; to update your browser, see
Update Google Chrome
.
In Chrome, visit
chrome://flags
.
At the top of the page, in the "Show flags" box, type
samesite
.
Next to "SameSite by default cookies", make sure the drop-down is set to
Default
.
More about cookies
How browsers use cookies
When a website needs to keep track of something about your interaction with the site (such as settings or preferences), it will often store a small text file called a cookie in your web browser's storage. Cookies allow websites to "remember" your settings in between browsing sessions, so that when you leave the site and come back later, the site will preserve your settings. This is a useful mechanism, and an extremely common part of how websites and web browsers work.
About third-party (or "cross-domain") cookies
Websites often embed external resources and experiences from other web materials served from another location on the web. Canvas, for example, may embed a learning tool inside a frame in the Canvas environment. These external web applications will sometimes need to store their own cookies. Since the external web application is being served from a different domain, or URL, than the one you see in the browser's URL bar, this cookie is considered to be third-party (or cross-domain).
How browsers handle third-party cookies
Since third-party cookies operate in a different domain than the main website that you may be visiting, some web browsers may block these cookies in some circumstances, depending on how the external application's cookies have been structured. Depending on how the third-party application is programmed, it may not function as expected, or it may fail to function entirely (with or without an error message). In short, the way an application behaves when the web browser blocks third-party cookies depends on the application's programming, and may vary.
