Overview
Approvals is a built-in approval process in Salesforce Marketing Cloud Content Builder that lets units establish processes for approving the content of email messages before they can be sent to recipients. Units decide which users can submit, review, and approve email content. When Approvals is enabled, all email content must be approved by a designated Content Approver. To use Approvals, an admin must turn on the feature for Content Builder; to get started, contact the Enterprise CRM Analysis and Adoptions team (
iucrmba@iu.edu
).
Workflow options
Two types of workflows are available in Content Builder Approvals:
Standard workflow:
The standard workflow features a Submitter, at least one Reviewer, and an Approver. Its statuses are Pending Submission, Submitted, Reviewed, Pending Resubmission, and Approved. The standard workflow proceeds as follows:
The Submitter creates content and submits it for review.
The Reviewer reviews the content and pushes it along to the approver.
The Approver approves the content or returns it for revision.
Two-step workflow:
The two-step workflow features only a Submitter and an Approver. Its statuses are Pending Submission, Pending Approval, Pending Resubmission, and Approved. The two-step workflow proceeds as follows:
The Submitter creates content and submits it for approval.
The Approver approves the content or returns it for revision.
The Enterprise CRM team recommends the two-step workflow for most use cases. Units can work with the Enterprise CRM Analysis and Adoptions team to determine which workflow option is the best fit.
Approvals considerations
Before you use Approvals with Content Builder, review these considerations:
When Approvals is initially enabled in a business unit, all existing emails are automatically approved.
If emails are going to be shared across business units, enabling Approvals in any of the business units involved in the sharing is not recommended, as approval requirements may be applied inconsistently.
Approvals can be disabled only by the Enterprise CRM team; for help, submit a ticket to
crmhelp@iu.edu
.
Instructions for Content Submitters
Most Marketing Cloud users will be assigned the Content Submitter role. Content Submitters are responsible for designing and creating email content. Once the content is ready to be sent, Content Submitters submit it to the appropriate team for review or approval. When an email is approved, any user with send permissions is able to proceed with completing the send.
Submit an email for approval
To submit an email for approval:
Create and save an email message.
Next to "Start Approvals Process", select
Start
.
Note:
If the
Start
button is grayed out, you will need to be added to a workflow team by your business unit's Content Approval Manager. For help identifying your business unit's Content Approval Manager, email
crmhelp@iu.edu
.
In the window that opens, enter additional information as follows:
Audience:
Select
Target Data Extension
or
Test Data Extension
. Reviewers and approvers will use this to preview the email message. This field is optional.
Instructions:
Provide any information the reviewer and/or approver should know when reviewing the send. This field is optional.
Team:
Select the appropriate approval workflow. This field is required.
Expected Completion Date:
Enter the date on which you need the approver to approve the email in order to proceed with the send as scheduled. This field is optional.
Select
Save and Submit
.
At this point, the email will have the "Pending Approval" status, and the approval process will move on to the next step in the workflow.
Check the status of an approval
To check the status of an approval, in the upper left, select
Home
, and then, under the "Content Builder" heading, select
Approvals
.
Submitted approvals and their statuses will be listed on the
My Approvals
tab. Select an approval to view details about the submission, including the preview that reviewers and approvers see and where the approval is within the workflow.
If you determine that further updates are needed to content you submitted, you can withdraw an approval, make the updates, and then resubmit. To withdraw an approval, open the approval, select the
Actions
drop-down at the top right, and then select
Withdraw
.
For approvals that are declined, you should review the comments and make any requested changes before resubmitting the content for approval.
For approved approvals, users with send permissions can proceed with sending the email via any method.
Instructions for Content Approvers
Content Approvers have permissions that allow them to review content, to submit content for approval, or to approve email content, depending on the workflow established by the business unit. The Content Approver role can be granted only by the Enterprise CRM team. To be granted this role, complete an
IU CRM User Access Request
and include the request for Content Approver permissions in the "Additional Information or Requests" field. Once the role is granted, the Content Approval Manager for the business unit is responsible for adding the new Content Approver to the workflow team. For help identifying a business unit's Content Approval Manager, contact
crmhelp@iu.edu
.
Review and approve an email
When an approval is submitted, the Approver or Reviewer is notified via email a new message is awaiting approval.
To approve an email, in the upper left, select
Home
, and then, under the "Content Builder" heading, select
Approvals
. To leave a comment, click anywhere within the email preview. Concise comments with explicit instructions for the submitter are recommended. After entering the comment, select
Save
.
The process for submitting a decision varies depending on the workflow:
Two-step workflow:
From the
Actions
menu, Approvers select
Approve
or
Decline
.
Standard workflow:
From the
Actions
menu:
Reviewers select
Complete
to send the approval to the next step in the workflow.
Approvers select
Submit comments
to request changes prior to approval or
Approve
to finalize the approval.
Edit a previously approved email
To edit a previously approved email, withdraw the email from Approvals, and then proceed with editing the email via Email Studio, Content Builder, or Journey Builder, as needed.
Note:
Pending or scheduled jobs will send using the originally approved email version, even if the email has been edited.
Notes on approvals for email sent via Journeys
To successfully validate a Journey, all emails in the Journey must be approved.
If the approval for an email used in a Journey is withdrawn, the email will send using the version that was approved when the Journey was activated.
If an email is updated via Email Studio or Content Builder and then approved, the Journey will need to be re-validated for changes to apply.
If an email is updated via Journey Builder and then approved, the Journey will send the most recently approved version.
Notes on approvals for email sent via Automation Studio
Automation Studio will allow an automation to be created and saved with an unapproved email but will error when the automation is run.
If the approval for an email used in an automation is withdrawn, the automation will error when run.
If there are multiple emails in the automation, the automation will error if any of the emails are not approved; even approved emails will not send.
Instructions for Content Approval Managers
Content Approval Managers are responsible for managing the approval process in their business unit. The Content Approval Manager role can be granted only by the Enterprise CRM team. To be granted this role, complete an
IU CRM User Access Request
and include the request for Content Approval Manager permissions in the "Additional Information or Requests" field.
As new users are added to a business unit, the Content Approval Manager is responsible for assigning them to the appropriate workflow teams.
Content Approval Managers can create additional teams as needed if different routing rules are required. For example, if all of Person A's content should be approved by Person B, but all of Person C's content should be approved by Person D, then two separate teams may be required.

To add or remove users from a team, select
Edit

Type a name or IU username into the "Assign a Workflow Role" field, check the box next to the role the selected user will be filling, and then select

.

Under the "Action" column, select

Open the Setup menu (in the upper right, select your name, and then select

In the "Assign a Team Name" field, choose a name that describes the purpose and group of users for which the workflow process is intended.
In the "Assign a Workflow Role" field, enter a user's name or IU username.

title: Use AdRx alerts for advisors and coaches
content:
Table of contents
Overview
Enterprise alerts
Dismiss or clear enterprise alerts
Campus custom alerts
View alerts

Insights tab on a student record

Overview
AdRx
Alerts gather important academic feedback in a single space to support advising and student success. The alerts include automated enterprise alerts that reset after each term and campus-specific custom alerts. You can easily access alerts from the
Advising Records
(
AdRx
)
landing page (Alerts card)
and via the
Insights tab
on the student's record. Advisors can
dismiss an alert
once they have taken appropriate action or if they believe it does not apply to them.
Important:
Students do not see alerts in their version of
AdRx
, the Student Online Advising Record (SOAR). When meeting with a student, be mindful when discussing the information provided by alerts.
Enterprise alerts
At the start of each fall, spring, and summer term, several alerts created by UITS run automatically. The information is refreshed daily and is useful for most advising units.
Default alerts you may see on a student's account
Alert
Description
Low early evaluation or current grade
A low grade means D+, D, D-, F, and, for Bloomington early evaluation, FM.
Negative SER feedback
There are over 50 observations and recommendations from SER that would trigger this alert.
Not enrolled full-time
The student has dropped all enrolled classes for the term.
SAS appointment not scheduled/completed
After the first week of the term, this alert is applied to any student who is assigned to you but has not scheduled via the Student Appointment Scheduler (SAS). The alert is automatically cleared the morning after you save the "Contact Note" from the meeting they scheduled via SAS.
Term withdrawn
The student has withdrawn from all classes.
Note:
An enterprise alert does not clear immediately after additional enrollment is processed or after an SAS appointment completes; the alert will be updated overnight.
Dismiss or clear enterprise alerts
In
AdRx
, enterprise alerts clear (expire) at the end of the term or when the alert is no longer valid. Some examples:
A student received negative SER feedback in a class, triggering a negative SER feedback alert. The student then receives new positive SER feedback in the same class, and the alert no longer displays.
A student begins the semester (or drops to) below full-time status, triggering an alert. The student then enrolls in additional hours to be full time, and the alert no longer displays.
Term-based alerts (that is, term withdrawal, below full-time enrollment, and not met with advisor yet) run in a nightly batch at 2am; these alerts will clear after the batch job runs the next morning.
The term boundary dates in
AdRx
are:
Spring term:
January 1 through May 15
Summer term:
May 16 through August 15
Fall term:
August 16 through December 31
When the end date for a custom alert has passed, students will automatically be removed from the alert. The alert's name will still display on the Alerts Management dashboard, but no students will be listed. This allows the alert to be reused with new dates and students.
Campus custom alerts
Campus-specific custom alerts are created by authorized users in the Alerts Management tool. These alerts can be applied to a group of students not readily available from
AdRx
or SIS (for example, a list of students who verbally express interest in a minor). The custom alert can be applied just before registration for the following term from that list.
Custom alerts appear in the same place as enterprise alerts; see the
View alerts
section below.
To see details about a custom alert, including why it was assigned to the student, select the alert's information icon (
). This will open a modal that displays additional information about the custom alert.
For information about creating custom alerts, see
Create and manage AdRx custom alerts for advisors
.
View alerts
You can view both custom and enterprise alerts on the
AdRx
landing page, within search and Caseload filters, and on the
Insights
tab.
AdRx
landing page
The
AdRx
Alerts card will by default display alerts for the advisor's assigned advisees; it includes the number of students for whom that alert applies.
To view alerts for an ad hoc Caseload group from this view, next to "Viewing", select the
Assigned Advisees
drop-down menu. The ad hoc Caseload groups display in order of creation date, from newest to oldest.
Filter in Caseload
For caseload groups and searches, both enterprise and custom filters are available to filter your list. Under the
Alerts
tab, you will see all current alerts available for either the ad hoc group, assigned advisees, or all of your campus, starting with current enterprise alerts and then custom alerts.
Insights tab on a student record
The
Insights
tab provides centralized access to important student engagement data and alerts to enhance advising conversations and promote advisor awareness of student academic performance. The
AdRx
Alerts card contains student academic information, such as negative SER feedback, low grade alerts from SER, and (over time) additional feedback that could signal ton an advisor that a student needs support or outreach.
Custom alerts in Caseload/advanced search
To view the list of students, on the
AdRx
dashboard, select the link for the custom alert. You can use the existing
AdRx
features such as creating a campaign from the list, adding contact notes, adding additional filters, etc.
Select the link for a specific student to view their Student Information page and Insights. The custom alert and the information icon (
) will display on the
Insights
tab.
Dismiss alerts
If you have taken action on the alert, or if the alert is not relevant to you, you can dismiss it. To remove the alert from your view of the student, next to the alert on the
Insights
tab (or the
AdRx
dashboard), select
Dismiss
.
Dismissing an alert does not remove it for other staff members who might be viewing the student in
AdRx
.

title: About the Canvas and Expand Provisioning app
content:
Table of contents
Overview
Launch and use the app
Overview
The Canvas and Expand Provisioning app is an
LTI tool
with a simple interface for uploading provisioning data for
Canvas
or
IU Expand
, Indiana University's non-credit elearning portal. At IU, campus units and external partners can use the tool to create courses, sections, enrollments, and canvas guest accounts in bulk, even if they lack the resources to fully automate the process. To request access to this service,
complete the Canvas/Expand Provisioning App and API Request form
.
Before using the tool, prepare your provisioning data files according to the guidelines in
Data specification for provisioning IU guests and non-credit courses, sections, and enrollments in Canvas and Expand
. Then, follow the instructions below to upload the files and optionally send custom notifications to new guest account recipients.
Important:
To create or update enrollments in a Canvas course, both the course and/or the course section must have SIS IDs. Courses and sections created through the Canvas user interface do not have SIS IDs. To add SIS IDs to manually created courses and sections, email the UITS LMS Development team at
lmsreq@iu.edu
.
Launch and use the app
After you have created your provisioning files, log into Canvas and navigate to
Canvas Provisioning
.
From the course navigation menu, select
Canvas and Expand Provisioning
.
In the
Department/Organization
drop-down, select the abbreviation for your unit.
Select
Upload file(s)
and select all files to be processed.
If you want to send custom notifications, check
Send custom notifications to new guest users?
.
Notes:
A generic notification with account confirmation and login instructions will be sent to all new IU guests listed in your
users.csv
file. The custom notification feature allows you to send a second, more specific notification to each guest. Use the custom notification to explain the purpose of the account, why it was created, by whom, etc.
The custom notification feature supports plain text messages only. Do not include any special formatting.
To avoid losing your message text, UITS recommends preparing the text in a word processor or plain text editor, then copying and pasting the text into the "Message Body" field on the custom notification screen.
A test version of the provisioning app is available. To access to the test version, go to
https://iu.test.instructure.com/courses/1887968
. Your provisioning changes will be reflected in courses in the Canvas test environment (

).
When using the Canvas test environment, do not upload a
users.csv
file with information for real external users. Doing so will send guest account invitations to each user for the
IU Login
test environment, which they should not be using. You can use your own personal email accounts for testing guest account creation in the test environment.
Also, note that you will not receive status notifications for provisioning jobs that run in the test environment. You will either need to manually spot check to validate the changes, or email the UITS LMS Development team at
lmsreq@iu.edu
for assistance with validation.
Select

If you checked
Send custom notifications to new guest users?
, the next screen will prompt you for the message details:
In the "Sender's Name" menu, select the name of the person who will be listed as the message sender.
Enter the subject of the message in the "Message Subject" field.
Type, or copy and paste, your message text into the "Message Body" field.

to view your custom message; select
Close
to close the preview.
When you are satisfied with the preview, select

The registered contacts in your unit will receive an initial notification and a second, more detailed notification after all the records have been processed in Canvas or Expand.
